external_articles.title: GitHub - ivanfioravanti/mlx-d1-gestures: Webcam to hand gesture and facial expression with Liquid AI's d1-2B on Apple Silicon (mlx-vlm), zero tokens generated
external_articles.body:
Your webcam in, hand gesture and facial expression out, live, on a Mac.

d1-2B by Liquid AI is a decision model, not a chat model. Each webcam frame gets four typed questions (which gesture? which expression? where is the hand? where is the face?), and one forward pass answers all of them with calibrated probabilities. It generates 0 tokens : all the work is prefill. On an M5 Max that is about 70 ms and ~600 input tokens per frame, roughly 14 decisions a second. It runs through mlx-vlm .

Everything stays on your Mac: the page and the model are served from 127.0.0.1 , and no frame is uploaded anywhere.

It starts decide.py and opens http://127.0.0.1:8049 once the model is ready (Ctrl-C stops it). Press Start camera and allow it. The first run downloads the model (2.2 GB). Prefer it by hand? uv run decide.py , then open the page.

Try thumbs up, thumbs down, OK, peace, open palm, pointing, a fist, a heart with two hands. Then smile, look sad or surprised, or put a hand on your chin to look like you're thinking. Hold each one still for a second, close to the camera.

To ask something else, edit QUESTIONS in decide.py . A choice question answers with one key of its criteria , and a box question answers with where the thing is. If you add or rename a key, also add its label to HAND / FACE in index.html .

The page has a three-way selector: MLX (the default), Core AI GPU and Core AI Neural Engine . The two Core AI backends run d1-2B exported from the PyTorch weights to Core AI as one fixed function, the 640×360 frame in and the answer logits for these four questions out. A small Swift worker runs it; decide.py starts it on first use and keeps it warm. POST /run?backend=mlx|coreai-gpu|coreai-ane picks the backend per request, and GET /status says which are available. Without the worker below, MLX works as before, and the Core AI buttons are disabled with the reason.

The two models are on Hugging Face, ivanfioravanti/d1-2B-gestures-CoreAI (LFM Open License v1.0, converted from LiquidAI/d1-2B ). decide.py downloads each one the first time you select it (3.1 GB each, then cached). All you build is the worker (Xcode 27):

To export the models yourself instead (uv, and a checkout of apple/coreai-models at ~/github/coreai-models ), then run with D1_COREAI_DIR=coreai/out :

The prompt is baked into the export. If you edit QUESTIONS , copy them into coreai/questions.py , export again from check_torch.py and run with D1_COREAI_DIR=coreai/out . Until then, the Core AI backends refuse with that reason. The Core AI export is traced at one shape, 16:9 (640×360, what the page sends from a 16:9 webcam). Core AI centre-crops other frame shapes, such as a 4:3 webcam or a square photo, to 16:9 before the model sees them. Its boxes are mapped back onto the whole frame, but anything outside the crop is invisible to it: a face cut by the crop gets a box that stops at the crop's edge. MLX takes every shape as it is.

Measured on an M5 Max (macOS 27.3) with the same frame. Each decision is timed from the picture to the answers (preprocessing, model, readout), median of 30 after 5 warm-ups. Model time is measured inside the Swift worker:

The Neural Engine build runs the whole graph on the Neural Engine. Its compiled plan is marked mps.fullyPlacedOnANE and mps.noGPUActivity . It is about 3× slower than the GPU for this 2B model but draws far less power: about 3.2 J per decision against 6.0 J for Core AI GPU and 8.4 J for MLX (whole Mac, above idle). Each MLP is computed in 8 chunks of its hidden channels, which made the Neural Engine 1.4× faster (from 236 to 171 ms); int8 weights did not help it. The first switch to it compiles for the Neural Engine, which takes about a minute once, and the request waits. After that, Core AI's cache makes it start in under a second. Its one miss on the test frames is a uniform mid-gray frame: same answers, but a probability off by 0.051, against the 0.05 tolerance. Every real frame matches. To match the GPU's numbers, the Neural Engine export needed exact rescalings of its weights: the Neural Engine loses precision on very small activations and its sigmoid is coarse. The model card lists every change. Int8 weights halve the size, but they bring no speedup on the GPU and don't keep parity on the Neural Engine, so they are not used.

With mactop installed ( brew install mactop ), two charts under the video show the last 60 s of the Mac's GPU and Neural Engine load and its power draw, one sample a second, camera on or off, with a mark at each backend switch. Stop metrics pauses them, and decide.py stops mactop a few seconds later. The figures cover the whole Mac, not just d1: macOS camera effects such as backgrounds also run on the Neural Engine, so turn them off in Control Center → Video Effects before comparing backends. Even with them off, an open camera keeps macOS camera processing busy on the Neural Engine, so for a clean comparison press Load video and pick a local movie instead: the page plays it (it never leaves the browser, only its frames go to decide.py ) and the camera stays closed. On an M5 Max the Neural Engine runs at 100% busy and about 35 W for the whole Mac, while either GPU backend draws about 130 W.

The model looks at one still frame at a time, so it sees poses, not movements: a wave or a nod would need a short clip. Subtle expressions are harder to read, so exaggerate them.

external_articles.title: Nvidia board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, source tells CNBC
external_articles.body:
Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.

The board is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity in order to discuss internal matters. Nvidia has hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead a probe into Huang's conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets.

Last week, Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company he founded, after 33 years as CEO. The resignation came days after Huang admitted to an affair, and news stories alleged he had an affair with Alice Huang, who worked for a customer and is alleged to have contact with Chinese intelligence, as well as affairs with employees at Nvidia.

Over the weekend, the Financial Times reported that Huang had discussed coming back with allies. Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday that Huang had not discussed a comeback with him.

A representative for Huang declined to comment on speculation on Sunday.

Many in the tech world have called for Huang to return as Nvidia CEO.

An online petition calling for his reinstatement has drawn 180,000 signatures as well as support from major figures including Elon Musk , Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.

President Donald Trump said on Monday that he is open to Jensen Huang returning as CEO of Nvidia.

"It was not put at risk, and our country is now stronger than ever before," Trump told reporters when asked about U.S. national security concerns.

On Friday, a representative for Nvidia's board said it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the Nvidia CEO role.

items.title: Does this change the AI Infra trade? Here’s how big the impact actually is: The US just slammed the door on Chinese AI labs quietly training on American chips from data centers in
items.body: Does this change the AI Infra trade? Here’s how big the impact actually is: The US just slammed the door on Chinese AI labs quietly training on American chips from data centers in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand. BIS closed the remote-access loophole. Near-term (0–6 months) Friction up for Chinese AI demand that was flowing through offshore rentals. Utilization pressure hits data centers in those hubs + compliance costs rise for operators (watch names with SEA exposure). Mild headwind for high-end GPU secondary demand. Not thesis-breaking for hyperscalers, but the gray channel is gone. Medium-term (6-18 months) Clear preference for US-controlled or fully compliant environments ($CRWV, $IREN, $NBIS). Large US operators and pure-play US AI Infra gain relative advantage. Frontier training gets pulled back onto US soil, where power is the real constraint ($VRT, $MOD, $OKLO). Second-order China doubles down on domestic silicon (Huawei Ascend etc.). Gap stays large, but the race turns more national. Reinforces power + grid as the ultimate chokepoint for the AI buildout. Policy support for domestic data centers and generation strengthens further. This is not a broad bearish signal for AI Infra. It’s a selective headwind for offshore/gray capacity and a tailwind for US-centric compute + the energy stack that powers it. The bottleneck was never chips. It’s still power, networking and memory.

items.title: Modeling Alphabet, Part 1: Search, Gemini, and YouTube
items.body:
With the busy period of this earnings season behind us, I have been meaning to take a fresh look at modeling two big tech companies, Meta and Alphabet. I would have started with Meta given my significant exposure, but decided to dig deeper into Alphabet first, as it may be one of the larger beneficiaries if Nvidia finds itself in a bit of turmoil in the post-Jensen world. The discussion on Alphabet’s position in the post-Jensen world will have to wait for tomorrow though, as Part 1 of this Alphabet modeling update will primarily focus on its very own **“problem child”**: Search!

Search may be the problem child, but it still pays most of the bills. Google Services, i.e. Search, the Gemini app, YouTube and subscriptions, is ~77% of Alphabet’s revenue this year, and it is ultimately what funds the capex buildout. It is also what lets Google stay at the frontier without having to worry too much about how much of its compute goes to inference or what each GW of it earns.

So I will go through all of Google Services today, with most of the time on Search. Part 2 tomorrow will cover Google Cloud, the cost of training Gemini, capex and valuation, and I will share the downloadable spreadsheet with it tomorrow.

[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!g6KB!,w_2400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F6e4584ec-2ae6-4553-bae2-615670cd2d15_1534x790.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!g6KB!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F6e4584ec-2ae6-4553-bae2-615670cd2d15_1534x790.png)

Sources: Company filings, MBI estimates

After 3Q’26 earnings, I [wrote](https://mbideepdives.substack.com/p/alphabet-3q26-search-worries-weighing?utm_source=publication-search) that Google is almost certainly destined to be a perennial share donor in the query market, and that what investors, including me, are really wondering is how much that will affect its numbers. This model is my attempt at an answer. **I have Google’s share of queries falling from ~76% today to ~52% by 2035, and Search still adding ~$32 Billion of revenue a year on average.** For context, Search added $6.8 Billion of revenue YoY in 3Q’26, or ~$27 Billion annualized, and that was a quarter that disappointed the market. So the model is basically assuming slightly faster growth than what 3Q’26 implied, mostly because ads are expected to arrive in the Gemini app.

[![Image 2](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!SkeU!,w_2400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F62fcd430-c13f-4eb7-918a-a7f8200d49e3_1177x1345.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!SkeU!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F62fcd430-c13f-4eb7-918a-a7f8200d49e3_1177x1345.png)

Sources: Company filings, MBI estimates

How can Google lose that much share and still grow?

Search revenue is paid clicks times cost per click. Let me break paid clicks drivers in three pieces: a) how fast the overall pie of queries grows, b) how much of that pie Google keeps, and c) how many ads get clicked per query.

Let me start with the query share question. Earlier this month, OpenAI [said](https://www.bigtechnology.com/p/openai-chatgpt-search-is-about-20) ChatGPT handles ~20% as many search-like queries as Google. I sized Gemini and the other AI assistants against ChatGPT using app and web usage data, added Bing and the other search engines, and Google (Search plus the Gemini app) comes out at ~76% of all search-like queries today. On the same math, it was ~81% in mid-2025. There is definitely some margin of error in this estimate, so I would treat these as ballpark numbers and **pay more attention to the direction**. Google gave up ~5 points of share in a little over a year.

And yet Google’s own query growth this year was the fastest in five years. Both can only be true if the pie itself is growing very fast, and the math implies search-like queries grew ~16-19% a year since mid-2025. That makes intuitive sense to me. People ask ChatGPT a lot of things they would never have typed into a search box. I assume the pie grows 17% next year and gradually slows to 8% by 2035.

Where does Google’s share go from here? **This is the most important assumption in Part 1, and admittedly it’s hard to be very confident about it**. New products tend to be adopted along an S-curve, so I didn’t want to draw a straight line. AI assistants went from ~14% of all queries in mid-2025 to ~21% today, and I let that curve run until it flattens at ~55%.

Why 55%? About half of Google searches are [informational](https://searchengineland.com/15-percent-google-searches-148-terms-448864), which is the kind of question assistants answer well, while about a third are navigational (think typing “amazon” into the search box) and are likely to stay within Google. I also assume Google keeps ~91% of the queries that stay with search engines, about where it has been since 2024, and that Gemini holds its current ~19% of assistant queries.

That takes Google’s share to ~59% by 2030 and ~52% by 2035, so **most of the loss comes in the next four years**. If assistants flatten at ~65% of queries instead of ~55%, Search revenue would be ~$48 Billion lower in 2035. If they stop at ~45%, it would be ~$50 Billion higher.

Even with that much share loss, Google’s own queries still grow ~10% next year and ~7% a year by 2035, simply because the pie grows faster than Google’s slice of it shrinks. Google ends up handling almost twice as many queries in 2035 as it does today. So volume is unlikely to be the problem, but the question remains how much Google will earn on each of those queries.

Google doesn’t disclose paid clicks per query, but you can back into it. If Google’s queries grew ~10% a year after ChatGPT’s launch, as Barclays [estimated](https://www.businessinsider.nl/chatgpt-isnt-slowing-down-google-just-yet-and-these-numbers-prove-it/), paid clicks per query was already falling ~4% a year in 2024 and 2025, before AI Mode even existed. Then in 3Q’26, paid click growth slowed to 8% while query growth hit a five-year high. I think the decline is likely to continue for a while. AI Mode queries are longer and more exploratory, and the ads have barely shown up there yet. They [reached](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/ads-in-ai-mode-global/) the first markets outside the US only late last month. So I have paid clicks per query falling ~4% next year, with the decline easing to ~2.5% by 2035 as the ads catch up.

For cost per click, I assume ~3-3.5% growth a year, close to what Google has averaged since 2022. You could perhaps argue for more. An AI query carries a lot more context than a few keywords, so ads should be better matched, and Microsoft says ads in Copilot [convert](https://ppc.land/microsoft-copilot-achieves-73-higher-click-through-rates-in-advertising-study/) 16% better than its search ads. But Google will no longer have ~90% of searches to itself. As queries spread across ChatGPT, Muse and other assistants, advertisers get more places to buy intent, and that may weigh on how much Google can charge.

Put the two together and revenue per query stays about flat through 2035, after growing ~1-3% a year in 2024-26. So query growth basically drives the search revenue in my model. These two assumptions matter as much as share does. Every point a year on either one is worth ~$47 Billion of Search revenue in 2035.

[![Image 3](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!q1QS!,w_2400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fa36e4908-7535-4d93-980c-1e428c4cb82e_1186x514.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!q1QS!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fa36e4908-7535-4d93-980c-1e428c4cb82e_1186x514.png)

Sources: Company filings, Barclays via Business [Insider](https://www.businessinsider.nl/chatgpt-isnt-slowing-down-google-just-yet-and-these-numbers-prove-it/), MBI estimates

Then there is the Gemini app, which doesn’t make any money from ads yet. Gemini subscriptions are part of Google One, which I will come back to later. The share math above gives it ~0.3 Trillion queries this year and ~2.4 Trillion by 2035. Management was quite clear on the 3Q call that ads have a place in agentic interfaces, so I assume ads arrive next year.

I also assume the ads ramp fast, to about half of what a search earns per query by 2030 and ~55% by 2035. Unlike OpenAI, Google doesn’t have to build an ad business from scratch. Ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode are served from advertisers’ existing [campaigns](https://www.seroundtable.com/google-ads-help-doc-ai-overviews-39469.html) with no opt-in, and Google says AI Overviews monetize at approximately the same rate as search, so the demand should be there as soon as Google turns ads on in the app. It probably won’t reach parity with a search though. People ask assistants fewer monetizable questions than they type into a search box, and an answer has less room for ads than a page of results. Each ad should be better targeted, but probably not enough to make up the difference. That gets me to ~$29 Billion of revenue by 2030 and ~$64 Billion by 2035, or ~12% of Search. It won’t make money right away though. By my estimate the app already costs Google ~$2.5 Billion a year in fixed costs, including payments to phone makers such as [Samsung](https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2025/04/22/google-paid-samsung-enormous-sums-for-gemini-ai-app-installs) to preinstall it. Once ads arrive, there are variable costs as well, mainly the share of ad revenue paid back to those phone makers and the cost of selling the ads, which I put at ~40% of the app’s revenue. So I have it losing money next year and reaching a ~50% margin by the early 2030s (before the AI compute which I treat separately below).

I would hold the Gemini app’s revenue very loosely. It is a bet on consumer behavior, which is hard to capture in a spreadsheet. We don’t know how people will split their time between Search, AI Mode and the Gemini app, and we know even less about how Google will make money once agents start doing the shopping, i.e. how much will come from ads, how much from fees on purchases and how much from subscriptions. I don’t model fees on purchases at all, so if agents end up completing a lot of purchases via Gemini or AI mode, there is likely upside here. OpenAI reportedly [projects](https://mobiledevmemo.com/how-can-chatgpt-reach-100bn-in-advertising-revenue/) ~$100 Billion of ad revenue for ChatGPT alone in 2030, which tells you how wide the range of outcomes is. What I have here is one reasonable path, but I wouldn’t claim high conviction on these numbers.

[![Image 4](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!LJsj!,w_2400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F7b777d72-14ae-4a05-ad7d-05d42f602677_1176x1426.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!LJsj!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F7b777d72-14ae-4a05-ad7d-05d42f602677_1176x1426.png)

Sources: Company filings, [ITU](https://www.itu.int/en/mediacentre/Pages/PR-2026-11-03-Facts-and-Figures.aspx), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/gabrielalinzainescu/2026/08/31/openais-chatgpt-ads-hit-1-billion-run-rate-in-just-200-days/), MBI estimates

What about margins? Alphabet doesn’t disclose Search’s margin, so I estimated margins for everything else in Google Services, and whatever is left is Search. That gives a ~58% operating margin this year. Google Services’ margin has expanded by more than a point a year since 2024, but I don’t want to extrapolate that as growth slows. I let Search’s margin rise ~0.3 points a year, which takes it to ~60% by 2035.

The obvious pushback is that AI answers cost a lot more to serve than ten blue links. So I modeled the compute behind AI Overviews, AI Mode and the Gemini app as its own cost line, and two things pull it in opposite directions. Each query will need a lot more computing, since more queries will get AI answers, the answers get longer and agents start doing multi-step tasks for you. Think of it as the number of tokens a model has to read and write to answer you, and I assume that rises ~28x per query by 2035. At the same time, better chips, smaller models and smarter serving software keep cutting the cost of each token, and I assume each GW of compute can handle ~11x more by then. That may sound aggressive, but Google cut the cost of AI Overviews queries by more than 90% in just 18 months.

On these assumptions, the bill goes from ~$4 Billion this year to ~$19 Billion in 2035, which is still less than 4% of what Google earns per query. Even if efficiency improves only ~20% a year instead of the ~30% I assume, the bill would be ~$40 Billion against ~$544 Billion of Search revenue. It is obviously a real cost, but I don’t think it dramatically changes the economics of Search.

[![Image 5](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!EQa7!,w_2400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Feaad9f62-e13f-47e8-b6fc-21e79102df56_1185x1158.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!EQa7!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Feaad9f62-e13f-47e8-b6fc-21e79102df56_1185x1158.png)

Sources: Company filings and earnings calls, MBI estimates

Okay, that’s about it for Search.

YouTube is relatively a bit simpler. Ad growth has slowed from ~15% in 2024 to ~11% this year, and every viewer who converts to Premium stops seeing ads. I fade growth from ~9% next year to ~7% by 2035, which doubles revenue to ~$88 Billion. It is **structurally** lower margin business than Search though. Creators keep ~55% of the ad revenue, and YouTube doesn’t disclose what it spends on anything else. So beyond the cost of storing and delivering all that video, I assume it spends about as much as Netflix does on R&D and overhead relative to revenue, and a bit less on sales and marketing since it doesn’t probably have to advertise as much for subscribers. That leaves YouTube ads with a ~16.5% operating margin, and since payout rates are contractual, I have it rising to just ~18.5% by 2035. YouTube TV passes most of its revenue on to the networks, so all of YouTube, including Music & Premium, comes to ~15% this year. That is a little below [MoffettNathanson’s](https://thewrap.com/youtube-worth-550-billion-moffettnathanson-note) estimate of ~16% for all of YouTube in 2025.

[![Image 6](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!JQTg!,w_2400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Feda12d23-928d-43ca-a02b-fc553c38b82b_1170x1405.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!JQTg!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Feda12d23-928d-43ca-a02b-fc553c38b82b_1170x1405.png)

Sources: [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/howyoutubeworks/youtubes-impact/), Company filings, MBI estimates

Google Network is about flat this year, but in 3Q’26 that took a 14% rise in price per impression to offset a 14% drop in impressions. I don’t think that will last, and I have it declining ~2% a year. At a ~10% margin after paying partners, it hardly matters either way.

Subscriptions, platforms and devices deserves more attention. It is already bigger than YouTube ads, and I have it almost doubling to ~$108 Billion. I model each product as subscribers times revenue per subscriber, and mostly just extend the recent pace of subscriber additions (table below).

The interesting one is Google One, which is where consumers pay for Gemini. It was [adding](https://9to5google.com/2025/05/15/google-one-150-million/) ~40 million subscribers a year, and probably more this year as the cheaper AI Plus plan rolled out. Going back to ~40 million takes it from ~235 million to ~595 million. What each of them pays is harder to call. More subscribers taking the AI plans should lift revenue per subscriber, but many of the new ones will likely come from markets such as India, where Google [sells](https://techcrunch.com/2025/12/10/google-launches-sub-5-ai-plus-plan-in-india-to-compete-with-chatgpt-go/) AI Plus for under $5 a month and has been [giving](https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/30/google-partners-with-ambanis-reliance-to-offer-free-ai-pro-access-to-millions-of-jio-users-in-india/) AI Pro away for 18 months to Jio customers. I don’t know which one wins, so I let revenue per subscriber rise just ~2% a year, from ~$34 to ~$41. Alphabet doesn’t disclose any of this, so the starting points are my estimates based on the milestones it has shared.

[![Image 7](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!2I6z!,w_2400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4a1497f9-8ebb-4ca4-b59b-f8ed00079227_1600x1216.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!2I6z!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4a1497f9-8ebb-4ca4-b59b-f8ed00079227_1600x1216.png)

Sources: Company filings, MBI estimates

Add it all up and Google Services grows ~8% a year, from ~$385 Billion this year to ~$765 Billion in 2035. Operating income doubles from ~$164 Billion to ~$347 Billion, and the margin edges up from ~43% to ~45% even after the AI compute bill.

[![Image 8](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!qe94!,w_2400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4a77c072-ad75-41a7-8c0c-69f36c662374_1161x1455.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!qe94!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4a77c072-ad75-41a7-8c0c-69f36c662374_1161x1455.png)

Sources: Company filings, MBI estimates

If I have to boil Part 1 down, six assumptions move the needle. Four of them drive Search, i.e. how fast total queries grow, where assistants’ share of those queries flattens, how many paid clicks survive as queries move to AI Mode and what happens to cost per click. The other two are how quickly the Gemini app monetizes and how fast the cost of serving an AI answer keeps falling. **A reasonable change in any one of them moves Google Services’ 2035 operating income by ~$20-30 Billion (~6-9%)**, far more than anything I assumed for YouTube or subscriptions. That may not sound like much, but **they can also go wrong together**. **If all six went against Google at once, 2035 operating income would be 36% below what I have here.****Of course, the same is true in the other direction.**

In Part 2 tomorrow, I will cover Google Cloud, where I would explore most of the growth, the capex debate and the post-Jensen question, along with the cost of training Gemini and valuation. I will share the full model with it so that you can change any assumption and see what it does.

items.body: $IREN is back to $16 a share today. That’s exactly the price I paid when I first bought the stock in July 2025. I genuinely thought I’d never see that price again. My position is now in the red, but I own significantly more shares than I did a year ago. And whenever I can, I keep adding. Even if AI CAPEX growth slows more than expected, even if Nvidia starts cutting prices or orders, I still believe the real bottleneck is elsewhere. You can manufacture more GPUs. But where are you going to plug them in? Power-ready data center sites don’t appear overnight. And $IREN happens to have exactly what the industry is struggling to secure. That’s why I’m still buying.

items.title: OPTICAL NETWORKING DAILY DIGEST, MONDAY, NOVEMBER 16, 2026 NEW PRODUCT • Astera Labs: Astera Labs and Hyve Solutions Corporation (a wholly owned subsidiary of TD SYNNEX) announced
items.body: OPTICAL NETWORKING DAILY DIGEST, MONDAY, NOVEMBER 16, 2026 NEW PRODUCT • Astera Labs: Astera Labs and Hyve Solutions Corporation (a wholly owned subsidiary of TD SYNNEX) announced an expanded collaboration on November 16, 2026: Hyve will integrate and deploy Astera's Orion Compute Board (Orion-CB), Orion Fabric Tray (Orion-FT), and Orion Link Board (Orion-LB) in its Hyve Solutions Apex rack-scale platform for neocloud and enterprise AI inference. Orion-CB scales up 8 PCIe accelerators and peripherals under a single fabric switch; Orion-FT is a common scale-up fabric for accelerators and memory pooling; Orion-LB extends fabric connectivity from tray to rack scale; Astera states Orion scales up to 160 accelerators in a pod. Hyve Apex systems featuring Orion are on track for availability in Q1 2027. Vendor testing cited in the release: a single Scorpio X-Series 320-lane switch delivered up to 89 percent higher tokens per second in an 8-GPU configuration versus two 144-lane switches. No financial terms and no part number were disclosed. https://t.co/EELnrTrkrg STATUS CHANGE • Marvell: Marvell and Penguin Solutions announced a strategic collaboration on November 16, 2026: (1) Marvell Structera X memory-expansion controllers are planned for Penguin Solutions SMART CXL add-in cards (PCIe 5.0 and CXL 2.0, recycling decommissioned DDR4), expected to be available for qualification and enterprise customer deployment by the end of 2026; (2) Marvell Photonic Fabric optical interconnect technology-based memory modules and NICs are being integrated into Penguin Solutions MemoryAI memory appliances and ComputeAI systems for low-latency, high-bandwidth, multi-rack disaggregated memory sharing and petabyte-scale memory pools, and joint development of Photonic Fabric integrated memory expansion servers is expected to sample in the second half of 2027. Separately, the Lumentum merger watch is unchanged: no Form S-4, no closing, and no new terms (4.500 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, $115 billion implied enterprise value, close guided H1 calendar 2028). https://t.co/jOcgyZGKol • NVIDIA: Lambda announced on November 16, 2026 the world's first large-scale deployment of co-packaged optics networking: NVIDIA Photonics switches connect more than 10,000 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs (GB300 NVL72 racks) at Lambda's Quebec campus, following early adoption first announced in November 2025. Each switch carries 144 ports at 800 Gb/s, liquid cooling, and 18 removable external light sources; benchmarks across rack, scalable unit, and pod configurations showed identical throughput and more stable signal integrity versus pluggable optics, with latency lower by 3.8 percent at rack scale growing to 10.1 percent at pod scale, and median optics temperature of 36C versus 51C for pluggable optics. No new product or part number was announced; the switches are the existing NVIDIA Photonics CPO family. NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 results remain scheduled November 17, 2026. https://t.co/ZhkhwKSxw2 • POET Technologies: POET Technologies reported third quarter 2026 results on November 16, 2026. Revenue was a record $1,026,087 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 80 percent from Q2 2026 ($569,925) and 244 percent from Q3 2025 ($298,434), the seventh consecutive sequential growth quarter and the first above $1 million. Net loss was $7,560,556, or $(0.04) per share, including a $6,378,235 non-cash warrant revaluation gain. Cash and short-term investments were $774.3 million at September 30, 2026; cash used in operations was $12.7 million. Product and status detail: 9 active customers and 16 projects, with 7 expected to enter production with POET engines in 2027; a $2.4 million purchase order from an existing unnamed customer in Q3 and a first purchase order from another leading Tier 1 laser manufacturer after quarter-end; Lumilens first products in assembly development, on schedule for verification this year; 1.6T optical engines scheduled to ramp to production in 2027; the backlog, including the 30,000 engines originally targeted for 2026, is now expected to ship by Q2 2027, with Q4 2026 shipments expected to exceed the first nine months of 2026 combined. Capacity: about 120 wafers per month in Malaysia in 2026 with tools committed toward about 1,250 to 1,500 per month, and Penang engine assembly in two phases completing end of 2027. Fourth quarter and full year 2026 results are scheduled for March 1, 2027 with the company's first quarterly conference call, reporting as a U.S. domestic issuer under U.S. GAAP from then. https://t.co/Z04VeT2zRr LIKELY PRODUCT • POET Technologies: POET Technologies named its Blazar hybrid laser in the Q3 2026 results release of November 16, 2026: sampling is planned for the first half of 2027 and production is targeted for early 2028. This is a vendor-stated roadmap item without full specifications, a part number, or a GA date, and it is tracked as likely, not confirmed. https://t.co/Z04VeT2zRr

external_articles.title: Hyve Solutions and Astera Labs Collaborate to Bring AI Inference Capacity to Customers Faster | FOX47
external_articles.body:
SAN JOSE, Calif. and FREMONT, Calif., Nov.  16, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Astera Labs, Inc. (Nasdaq: ALAB), a leader in semiconductor-based connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI infrastructure, and Hyve Solutions Corporation, a U.S.-based design and manufacturing partner for compute, storage, and networking systems in AI, cloud, and digital infrastructure, and a wholly owned subsidiary of TD SYNNEX Corporation (NYSE: SNX), today announced an expanded collaboration to help neoclouds and enterprises bring AI inference capacity online faster. Hyve will offer Astera Labs’ Orion Compute Board, Fabric Tray, and Link Board as part of the Hyve Solutions Apex platform at rack scale. Because the components are pre-validated within Astera Labs’ compute-agnostic reference architecture, customers can expect shorter integration and qualification cycles and the flexibility to choose the accelerators and CPUs that best fit their cost, lead time, and workload.

Hyve Solutions Apex platform offers Astera Labs’ Orion line:

Hyve's Apex platform brings Orion's single-hop Scorpio fabric to customer deployments. In Astera Labs testing of an 8-GPU configuration, a single Scorpio X-Series 320-lane switch delivered up to 89% higher tokens per second than a baseline built on a conventional two-switch configuration, [1] helping operators lower their cost per token. Apex systems are air-cooled, so customers can deploy Orion in existing data centers without liquid-cooling infrastructure, and Hyve's future-ready chassis is designed to support higher-power accelerators as they arrive.

"Every GPU is waiting on something, and too often it is the fabric," said Pravin Patel, vice president and general manager of the AI Platform Solutions Group at Astera Labs. "Thanks to Astera Labs’ advanced in-network compute and Hypercast™ features available in the Orion architecture, Orion is designed to let customers scale up to 160 accelerators in a pod with predictable, low-latency communication. Hyve turns that into a deployable chassis, and customers can engage with Hyve today to get better cost per token.”

“The rack is now the unit of AI, and rack-level systems are what Hyve builds,” said Dr. Dimitris Ziakas, chief technology officer and vice president of Architecture at Hyve Solutions. “We design, integrate, validate, and deploy at rack scale. Pairing Hyve Apex with Astera Labs’ Orion gives customers scale-up AI that they can deploy once and evolve over time, swapping accelerators as their workloads change without rebuilding the system.”

Hyve Apex systems featuring Orion rack-scale reference architecture are on track for availability in the first quarter of 2027. Contact Hyve Solutions at www.hyvesolutions.com or connect with Astera Labs for commercial inquiries.

external_articles.title: Marvell and Penguin Solutions Collaborate to Address Data Center AI Memory and Accelerate Inference at Scale
external_articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. – November 16, 2026 – Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL), a leader in data infrastructure semiconductor solutions and Penguin Solutions, Inc . (NASDAQ: PENG), the AI Factory Platform Company, today announced a strategic collaboration to address AI memory demands. This collaboration brings together two complementary technologies: CXL-based memory expansion that enables data centers to extend server memory capacity using existing DDR4 memory, and advanced photonic technology designed to enable high-bandwidth, low latency memory sharing across multiple racks.

As AI workloads shift from model training to large-scale inference and agentic AI, memory capacity, bandwidth, and latency are becoming critical constraints on application performance and token economics. Growing model sizes, longer context windows, and expanding KV-cache requirements are driving memory needs into hundreds of gigabytes and increasingly terabytes per node. These demands are accelerating the shift beyond traditional server-attached memory toward memory expansion, pooling, and disaggregation technologies such as CXL and optical shared-memory fabrics, enabling memory capacity to scale independently of compute.

Two Complementary Levels of Memory Expansion

Marvell and Penguin Solutions are developing two complementary memory expansion technologies designed to address AI infrastructure needs at the server and pod levels:

These two technologies are highly complementary. Direct-attach memory expansion addresses immediate, server-level capacity needs today, while multi-rack photonic memory sharing is designed to enable high-bandwidth, low-latency memory sharing across multiple racks to support increasingly demanding AI workloads. Together, these approaches are designed to provide customers with greater flexibility to expand memory capacity and scale AI infrastructure as its needs evolve, offering a single upgrade path from direct-attach expansion to disaggregated, multi-rack sharing, without re-architecting their infrastructure at each step.

An additional benefit of the standard AIC form factor is its ability to support memory expansion beyond direct server attachment. A Structera X-powered Penguin SMART CXL add-in card can be used to build dedicated CXL memory appliances, allowing operators to pool recycled DDR4 capacity for disaggregated allocation across multiple hosts, not just within a single server.

“AI memory demand is growing rapidly, while adding new memory production capacity takes time and substantial investment. Elevated memory prices are also increasing the cost of scaling AI infrastructure,” said Jihoon Han, senior technology and market analyst, Memory, at Yole Group. “This creates a need for solutions that bridge the gap by making better use of available memory resources. Memory expansion and pooling, supported by optical interconnects to help manage latency as pools scale across racks, offer a promising option for meeting growing capacity needs while managing costs over the next few product cycles.”

“For AI inference to scale, it requires delivering tokens at a higher economic efficiency,” said Preet Virk, senior vice president and general manager, Photonic Fabric Business Unit at Marvell. “Marvell is a leader in memory expansion with an unmatched portfolio of products. By combining CXL-based memory expansion with a roadmap to optical memory sharing, Marvell and Penguin Solutions are giving CIOs and AI data center leaders a practical path to improve accelerator utilization which directly leads to increased token revenue, eases pressure from constrained HBM and DDR5 supply and builds more flexible AI memory architectures without wholesale infrastructure replacement.”

“As inference and agentic AI workloads accelerate in data centers, memory is becoming increasingly critical to the performance and economics of AI factories,” said Kash Shaikh, president and CEO of Penguin Solutions. “Our expertise at the intersection of AI infrastructure and memory uniquely positions us to address these evolving demands. Through our collaboration with Marvell, we are advancing our memory innovation roadmap with CXL-based memory and advanced photonic solutions designed to address the memory bottlenecks. We expect this to strengthen our Full-Stack AI Factory Platform to help customers scale data center AI infrastructure efficiently and maximize the return on their AI investments.”

Penguin SMART CXL add-in cards powered by Marvell Structera X memory-expansion controllers are expected to be available for qualification and enterprise customer deployment by the end of 2026. Joint development with Photonic Fabric integrated memory expansion servers are expected to sample in the second half of 2027.

To learn more about Marvell and Penguin Solutions, visit Marvell Booth #4003 at Supercomputing26 , November 16-20, McCormick Place, Chicago.

To deliver the data infrastructure technology that connects the world, we’re building solutions on the most powerful foundation: our partnerships with our customers. Trusted by the world’s leading technology companies for over 30 years, we move, store, process and secure the world’s data with semiconductor solutions designed for our customers’ current needs and future ambitions. Through a process of deep collaboration and transparency, we’re ultimately changing the way tomorrow’s enterprise, cloud and carrier architectures transform—for the better.

Penguin Solutions is the AI Factory Platform Company. We design, build, and manage next-generation data centers for enterprises, sovereign AI initiatives, and AI cloud providers.

external_articles.title: POET Technologies Reports Record Q3 2026 Revenue of $1.03M, Up 244%
external_articles.body:
November 16, 2026 07:00 ET | Source: POET Technologies Inc. POET Technologies Inc.

TORONTO, Nov.  16, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- POET Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ: POET) ("POET" or the "Company"), a leading designer and developer of photonic integrated circuits, light sources and optical engines for data center and AI networks, today reported record revenue of $1,026,087 for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 80% from the second quarter of 2026 and 244% from the third quarter of 2025. It was the Company's seventh consecutive quarter of sequential revenue growth. Net loss was $7.6 million, or $(0.04) per share, improved from $11.3 million, or $(0.07) per share, in the second quarter of 2026 and from $9.4 million, or $(0.11) per share, in the third quarter of 2025. Cash and short-term investments were $774.3 million at quarter-end, and cash used in operations during the quarter was $12.7 million. The Company's unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis for the quarter have been filed on SEDAR+ and as exhibits to a Form 6-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission via EDGAR. All figures are in U.S. dollars.

"Our first quarter above a million dollars in revenue, and seven straight quarters of growth, come from programs we spent years building and are now moving into production," said Dr. Suresh Venkatesan, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. "In the quarter we signed a development agreement with a Tier 1 laser company for an external light source engine and received a $2.4 million purchase order from an existing customer. We are scaling capacity approximately tenfold in both wafers and engine assembly to serve the seven of our nine active customers we expect to move into production in 2027, and we have grown the team to 164 people to run it."

"We expect to ship our current backlog of optical engines, including the 30,000 engines we had targeted for 2026, by the second quarter of 2027, as the capacity we have already funded comes online," Dr. Venkatesan added. "Like much of the industry, we have faced supply chain tightening, wafer and component shortages, and are working through a yield ramp of a new production technology this year. We have secured roughly ten times our existing wafer capacity and are installing the equipment now. Until it is in place, we are sequencing wafer starts between production orders and new customer programs, so we ship to our customers' schedules and keep our new products on track. Our shipments in the current quarter will exceed those of the first nine months of the year combined."

"We have the balance sheet to build at scale and the customer programs to build for," Dr. Venkatesan added. "With Giovanni Pacelli joining as Chief Financial Officer, it’s time to report on that progress on a regular basis, beginning with our first quarterly earnings call on March 1, 2027."

"POET ended the quarter with $774.3 million in cash and short-term investments," said Giovanni Pacelli, Chief Financial Officer. "The reported net loss narrowed in part because of a $6.4 million non-cash gain on the revaluation of warrants. Cash used in operations was $12.7 million, essentially unchanged from the second quarter. Beginning with our fourth-quarter and full-year results on March 1, 2027, POET will report as a U.S. domestic issuer, with financial statements prepared under U.S. GAAP."

Net loss for the quarter was $7,560,556, or $(0.04) per share, compared with $11,338,060, or $(0.07) per share, in the second quarter of 2026 and $9,369,714, or $(0.11) per share, in the third quarter of 2025. The quarter's results include non-cash items of $5.7 million of stock-based compensation, $1.1 million of depreciation and amortization, a $6.4 million gain on the revaluation of the derivative warrant liability and $122,000 of non-cash finance costs. The warrant revaluation produced a $5.5 million gain in the second quarter of 2026 and a $2.4 million loss in the third quarter of 2025. Cash used in operations was $12.7 million, compared with $12.2 million in the second quarter of 2026. Research and development expense was $5.4 million, compared with $5.8 million in the second quarter, with quarter-to-quarter changes reflecting the timing of development programs and production readiness activities. Cash and short-term investments were $774.3 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $796.3 million at June 30, 2026.

Net loss excluding warrant revaluation is a non-IFRS measure that removes the non-cash change in the fair value of the derivative warrant liability from reported net loss. The Company presents it because the warrant revaluation moves with the share price and does not reflect operations. The measure retains other non-cash items and does not measure cash used in operations. This non-IFRS measure is presented for supplemental informational purposes only. Non-IFRS financial measures should not be considered a substitute for financial information presented in accordance with IFRS. There are limitations in using this non-IFRS financial measure because it has no standardized meaning under IFRS and may differ from similarly titled measures used by other companies. The reconciliation to reported net loss follows.

The following table summarizes the Company's results for the five most recent quarters. The Company's financial statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis have been filed on SEDAR+ on November 16, 2026.

The Company expects to ship its current backlog of optical engines, including the 30,000 engines originally targeted for 2026, by the second quarter of 2027, in line with customer delivery schedules and as its new wafer and engine assembly capacity comes online. Fourth-quarter shipments are expected to exceed the Company's total shipments for the first three quarters of 2026, with production running well ahead of shipments to build engines against customer orders for delivery in the first half of 2027. The new engine assembly line is targeted to be manufacturing-ready by mid-2027, Blazar sampling is expected to begin in the first half of 2027, and seven of the Company's nine active customers are expected to enter production with POET engines in 2027. Production timing for each program depends on customers completing qualification of POET engines within their own modules, which can require design changes to the customer's module or, at times, to the Company's engine; longer industry lead times can extend these design cycles. The Company is aligning its production plans with its customers' delivery schedules. The Company will report its fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 results on March 1, 2027 and will host its first quarterly conference call that day. The Company will report progress on each program as milestones are reached.

POET is a design and development company offering high-speed optical engines, light source products and custom optical modules to the artificial intelligence systems market and to hyperscale data centers. POET's photonic integration solutions are based on the POET Optical Interposer™, a novel, patented platform that allows the seamless integration of electronic and photonic devices into a single chip using advanced wafer-level semiconductor manufacturing techniques. POET's Optical Interposer-based products are lower cost, consume less power than comparable products, are smaller in size and are readily scalable to high production volumes. In addition to providing high-speed (800G, 1.6T and above) optical engines and optical modules for AI clusters and hyperscale data centers, POET has designed and produced novel light source products for chip-to-chip data communication within and between AI servers, the next frontier for solving bandwidth and latency problems in AI systems. POET's Optical Interposer platform also solves device integration challenges across a broad range of communication, computing and sensing applications. POET is headquartered in Toronto, Canada, with operations in Singapore, Penang, Malaysia and Shenzhen, China. More information about POET is available on its website at www.poet-technologies.com .

items.title: Take: You can tell a lot about someone by how they treat waiters at a restaurant. There is a near 100% correlation between (1) rudeness and tipping bad and (2) being an awful perso
items.body: Take: You can tell a lot about someone by how they treat waiters at a restaurant. There is a near 100% correlation between (1) rudeness and tipping bad and (2) being an awful person. The finance industry equivalent is how you treat exiting employees and their deferred compensation. The unwritten rule is that when people show respect on the way out, you treat them with respect too. Outside of rare instances, clawing back deferred compensation is a red line. Additionally, while non-competes have a role in business, forcing a mid-level employee to sit out for a year [or more] because of “competitive reasons” is non-sensical. The craziest thing I ever saw was a $500k a year analyst have to “hide” for a year from his former hedge fund. He skipped every conference, had an assumed name on his Bloomberg terminal and didn’t even have a company email account. When he finally showed up a year later on the industry circuit, he was hunted down by his prior boss (who was worth several hundred million mind you) and yelled at in public for “being a backstabbing liar.” Anyways, on an unrelated note, a lot of people in the finance industry don’t like the Commerce Secretary.

items.body: The $NVDA guide tomorrow could cause a lot of uncertainty, and I do not think people are ready for it. This is an interim CEO’s first print. Interim leadership almost never swings big on a guide, the playbook is conservative, guide wide, lower the bar you just inherited, leave room to beat later. Kress is a career CFO on top of it, careful is her default setting. Do not be surprised by a wider range than the tight band they have given for years, or less detail than usual. The problem is this market cannot tell the difference between caution and confession right now. A conservative first guide is completely normal corporate behavior, but after the month $NVDA just had, a soft or wide number gets read as confirmation of every fear out there. That is how you get violent moves off a quarter that was actually fine. Either way, expect uncertainty into and out of this one.

items.title: https://t.co/CYB0vLZOxi TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10PM TO 10AM on 11/16/26 In this window the first government act in the case landed. The Commerce Department's Bu
items.body: https://t.co/CYB0vLZOxi TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10PM TO 10AM on 11/16/26 In this window the first government act in the case landed. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule closing the remote access channel at the center of the Megaspeed business model, and imposed a new destination license requirement covering Singapore and Malaysia, Megaspeed's two operating jurisdictions. The Straits Times reported the first known enforcement action in Indonesia linked to the case, a police search of Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary that found empty server racks and no chips. President Trump publicly welcomed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive, in the opposite direction from his Treasury secretary's push for an outside chief executive. THE RULE IS ISSUED • On November 16, 2026, the Bureau of Industry and Security released an interim final rule, "Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors" (RIN 0694-AK50). The press release states the rule was "written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council." • The rule's new end-use control, new EAR section 744.24, requires a license for exports, reexports, or transfers of advanced super-intelligence semiconductors when there is knowledge the items are destined for use in data centers, wherever located, that will provide direct or indirect access to a significant volume of computing power, more than 12,000,000 aggregate TPP, to or for an entity headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent is headquartered in, Macau or a Country Group D:5 destination, which includes China. • Data centers already providing such access before publication must obtain a license within 90 days of the rule's effective date or face future export restrictions. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters must perform robust due diligence on customers, including direct or indirect ownership or control by D:5 or Macau persons. The license requirement does not apply to commercial recommender systems. • The rule is effective on its Federal Register publication date, which the display copy leaves to be inserted, so the 90-day clock's start is not yet datable from the documents read. Comments are due 60 days after publication. • In the same rule, a license will now be required to export, reexport, or transfer advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil, countries the rule identifies as presenting a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The requirement does not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met. • Applications are reviewed case by case, with destinations evaluated on the effectiveness of their export-control regimes and their coordination with BIS. Commerce states it will actively monitor for countries that tolerate evasion and will consider consequences including import restrictions, further license requirements, downgrading a country's status, and Entity List designations. • The rule also amends the presumptions front-end chip fabricators and packagers face when exporting advanced-node logic chips, reducing pathways to overcome them for designers in license-required destinations, and it formally rescinds the regulations implementing the AI Diffusion Rule. • The issued rule names five countries. The November 14 reporting in the record, attributed to The Information, carried a seven-country list for the rule in preparation that also included Norway and South Africa; neither is in the rule as issued. Megaspeed itself is not named in the rule and remains off the Entity List. THE INDONESIA SEARCH • The Straits Times reported on November 16, 2026 that officers of the Indonesian National Police's Criminal Investigation Department, Bareskrim, searched the premises of PT Megaspeed International Indonesia, the Indonesian subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed International, earlier in 2026, as part of an inquiry requested by the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation to trace Nvidia chips bought by Megaspeed, and found server racks at the site but no graphics processing units. The racks appeared never to have been unpacked or used, suggesting the chips were never installed there. • The paper calls the search the first known enforcement action in Indonesia linked to the case. Its source for the search is a senior Indonesian government official who requested anonymity because he is unauthorised to speak to the media. Inspector General Untung Widyatmoko, head of the Indonesian National Police's International Relations Division, declined to comment, and Bareskrim head Commissioner General Asep Safrudin did not reply to the paper's queries. The search is carried at that grade: a named outlet's reporting resting on a single anonymous official source, not yet corroborated. • The correspondent's own checks of November 13, reported in the same article, found the subsidiary's listed address, fifth floor, Cyber 1 building, No. 8 Jalan Kuningan Barat, South Jakarta, is not on the building's tenant list; a receptionist and a MettaDC officer confirmed it operates out of PT MettaDC Teknologi Indonesia's office there, and it also rents space in the Jababeka Industrial Estate in Cikarang, Bekasi, West Java, a facility owned by PT HDC. • In the same report, the same anonymous senior official alleged that most of the Nvidia hardware bought by Megaspeed entities was likely shipped to Indonesia, and that investigators believe much of it was then sent on to China, possibly by private jet. The article gives no GPU quantity, no flight details, and no intermediaries for this alleged movement, and carries no public finding that Megaspeed broke export rules. It is carried as an allegation, not as an established route. TRUMP WELCOMES A RETURN • President Donald Trump, asked by a reporter on November 16, 2026 whether he wants to see Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, answered verbatim: "I would not mind that. I like, you know, I threw out the name of Tim Cook, but I would say that Jensen's reinstatement - if he learns a big lesson, I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another - but I would certainly not mind seeing that." • No prior claim in the record has Trump publicly stating he would not mind, or would welcome, Huang's reinstatement. He previously floated Tim Cook as Huang's successor on November 12, and said on November 9 that Huang had told him he had no idea Alice Huang was a spy and that he believed him. • The statement cuts against Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's on-the-record push for a dramatic shakeup and an outside chief executive, with a 10-day board answer deadline. It is a presidential stance, not an act: the board decides, and no board statement accompanied it. THE CHECKPOINTS • November 17: Nvidia earnings, and the Warren and Coons records preservation confirmation is due. • November 18: the briefing track. • November 24: Bennet's answers due. • About November 25: Bessent's 10-day deadline for answers from Nvidia's board and outside counsel on export-compliance culture. • December 1: Huang's closed-door transcribed interview before the three House committees, date not locked, and the House Foreign Affairs Democrats' answers due. • December 2: Teter's requested closed-door transcribed interview. • December 3: Scott's requested public Senate Banking hearing with Huang, and the Foreign Affairs hearing with Under Secretary Kessler at 10 a.m. • December 10: Scott's requested public Senate Banking hearing with Lutnick.

external_articles.title: Jensengate | Atlas Peak Research
external_articles.body:
The fall of Jensen Huang at Nvidia, tracked in twelve-hour editions: the newest edition in full at the top, and every earlier edition in the archive below.

TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10PM TO 10AM on 11/16/26

In this window the first government act in the case landed. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule closing the remote access channel at the center of the Megaspeed business model, and imposed a new destination license requirement covering Singapore and Malaysia, Megaspeed's two operating jurisdictions. The Straits Times reported the first known enforcement action in Indonesia linked to the case, a police search of Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary that found empty server racks and no chips. President Trump publicly welcomed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive, in the opposite direction from his Treasury secretary's push for an outside chief executive.

In this window the succession fight split in public on the same Sunday shows that moved the congressional track. Jensen Huang has agreed to a closed-door interview with the three House committees, with no subpoena needed and the date still being discussed. A briefed Gang of Eight member said on the record that the intelligence community does not know whether Alice Huang was a witting asset. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent directed the board toward an outside chief executive and set it a 10-day deadline to answer on export-compliance culture, while the Financial Times reported Huang himself is discussing a comeback, with an ally war room lobbying for his return.

In this window the channel record widened again: the Wall Street Journal reported records showing Megaspeed arranged to send nearly $12 billion of top Nvidia chips to companies in China, a fifth chip figure with its own window, and reported an unwritten Nvidia rule capping partners' Chinese customers and a new channel node, Aolani Cloud. Megaspeed answered publicly for the first time on Alice Huang, saying she left the company effective August 30, 2025 and that it has retained outside counsel for an internal investigation. The Washington Post reported Huang is quietly helping pick his own successor, and Elon Musk said many of Nvidia's supply deals were a handshake with Huang personally.

In this window the fight over the classified memo at the center of the case widened: the Washington Post reported the memo was Secretary of State Marco Rubio's recasting of a CIA report in more assertive terms, and CNN reported the CIA is not yet convinced the intercepts prove Alice Huang knowingly funneled information to Beijing. The Financial Times reported Nvidia carries directors and officers insurance that protects its directors personally and not the company, filings show a director sold about $946.6 million of stock in the weeks before the board inquiry opened, and Reuters reported Chinese AI firms are racing to reserve Nvidia powered capacity outside China before the remote rental loophole closes. South Korea said Nvidia has reconfirmed its 260,000 GPU supply plan after the resignation, Bill Ackman defended Huang on presumption of innocence grounds, and the first Sunday show booking for a case chair was announced for tomorrow.

Overnight, Reuters reported that Jensen Huang told Nvidia's own general counsel and chief marketing officer in writing that his interactions with Alice Huang and Megaspeed were standard business dealings, the House chairs' 8 p.m. deadline for his written acceptance of the December 1 interview passed with nothing public, and a filings-based reconstruction put $5,353 million of Nvidia's formerly Singapore-billed revenue with China and Hong Kong headquartered buyers. Super Micro denied on the record that Megaspeed was ever its customer, a sitting administration official argued Huang should have been warned the way a congressman once was, and the street kept repricing the overhang: HSBC cut its target by more than half, and a billionaire holder said he will make no further investment in Nvidia without Huang.

Today the fight over the Megaspeed Entity List delay became an open cabinet split, the Commerce Secretary's own tenure came into question, Reuters documented the scale of Chinese AI projects built around restricted Nvidia chips, and the succession search moved in public for the first time: the board was reported to have approached an external candidate, then issued its first statement calling candidate speculation premature, while two major holders asked the board to slow the process down and keep Jensen Huang's return on the table. The 8 p.m. deadline for Huang's written acceptance of the December 1 interview passed with nothing public.

THE SUCCESSION SEARCH MOVES, THEN THE BOARD PUSHES BACK

Overnight, the House turned its request to Jensen Huang into an ultimatum with a deadline tonight, the Senate Banking subpoena threat was verified from the letter itself and shown to run to Huang only, Bloomberg published the first account of how the admission and the resignation decision actually happened, Malaysia opened its own official inquiry into the Megaspeed channel while its prime minister said there is no indication so far that chips were exported from Malaysia, and CNN's reporting reframed the Alice Huang spy question toward recruitment after access.

The first full day after Jensen Huang's resignation widened the case on every front at once. Huang agreed to testify before Congress, the Senate Banking Committee requested dated public hearings for Huang and for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, the tax committees opened their own investigation with a records preservation demand, the Justice Department spoke on the record for the first time, Singapore published its full account of the Alice Huang investigation, and the channel record added two new end points, DeepSeek and Huawei.

THE TAX COMMITTEES OPEN AN INVESTIGATION

The case resolved overnight. Nvidia announced this morning that Jensen Huang has resigned, effective immediately, ending the board process that had built through the night: Semafor had reported some directors favored CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, and Kress is the interim appointment in the release. The night also deepened the record behind the case, with the Wall Street Journal's account of the husband who introduced Huang to Alice Huang, Congress turning its fire on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Megaspeed's first public statement, and the analyst downgrade wave broadening before the announcement landed.

In twelve hours the case moved from congressional pressure to the boardroom. The New York Times reported a second extramarital relationship, this one with a direct report. The Wall Street Journal reported the board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang, and Bloomberg reported a succession search is under way. The committees' 5 PM deadline for his answer on the November 18 briefing passed with no acceptance or alternative date reported, and the desk raised its exit estimate in this window.

Atlas Peak Research. Compiled from public reporting, company statements, and congressional and court records. Each edition covers twelve hours of the case and appears here in full.

Updated 11/16/26 10:07 AM ET · 10 editions

external_articles.body:
探針卡暨測試設備廠旺矽 （6223） 16日於法說會表示，預估2027年營收至少成長50%，毛利率維持六成以上，費用率落在23%至25%；第4季營收估季增5%至10%，毛利率與第3季相仿。

旺矽指出，訂單能見度較三個月前改善，一家大型雲端服務供應商（CSP）已明確表示，下一世代AI產品將提高旺矽的供應比重，出貨量也將放大。目前正與客戶對接明年專案，部分合作已延伸至2028年，既有客戶需求仍未完全滿足，新客戶也持續排隊接洽。

為支應需求，2026年底VPC、MEMS月產能預計分別達200萬針、350萬針，明年底增至至少250萬針、600萬針。新增產能將逐季開出，年底更新計畫時仍有上修空間，2028年也將維持積極擴產。

美系CPU大廠合作將先從筆電CPU切入，再逐步拓展其他產品線。湖口PCB廠維持明年下半年投產目標，透過探針與關鍵零組件自製，降低外部供應鏈依賴，提升交貨彈性。

CPO方面，Insertion 2預計今年12月取得首家客戶認證結果，另與第二家大型國際客戶接洽；Insertion 3已向三家客戶交付工程機，另三家將陸續交機，預期明年上半年逐步迎來量產機訂單。公司強調，兩者對應不同測試階段，Insertion 2不會被取消或整併。

兩款設備單機報價均約100萬美元，考量至少六個月交期及後續驗收，明顯營收貢獻預期落在2028年。配合CPO組裝場地明年第1季啟用及客戶陸續導入，公司看好2028年CPO設備營收占比可達雙位數百分比。

items.title: The open-source LLM ecosystem could really benefit from an LLM building-block API. We have so many LLM components across different models now. Whether you are using PyTorch or C++
items.body: The open-source LLM ecosystem could really benefit from an LLM building-block API. We have so many LLM components across different models now. Whether you are using PyTorch or C++ and CUDA code directly, there is a major switching cost when you want to run experiments or ablation studies, say swapping GQA with MLA, dense FFNs with MoE, attention layers with Mamba2 or Gated DeltaNet, or standard residual connections with attention residuals. Currently, it’s very messy even with LLM-assisted coding. It could maybe be on top of PyTorch or CUDA directly, but it needs to be carefully engineered and maintained (versus quickly vibe-coded on a weekend) and efficient enough that people trust it to use in production (which is really a requirement to move beyond toy examples). Maybe some food for thought for a big, well-funded lab :) (There are some efforts that go into that direction, like torchtitan, torchtune, Megatron Core, OLMo-core, but they are not quite that level of abstraction, I'd say. And, as always, there’s the chicken-and-egg problem: it needs to be popular to get widely adopted, and it needs to get widely adopted to become popular.)

items.title: What would happen to $NVDA earnings multiple if investors could sleep well? We can learn a little bit by looking at what’s happened with $AAPL’s multiple over the past 15 years. Se
items.body: What would happen to $NVDA earnings multiple if investors could sleep well? We can learn a little bit by looking at what’s happened with $AAPL’s multiple over the past 15 years. Setting aside all of the near-term transition risk. During the iPhone’s hypergrowth phase from 2009 to 2011, AAPL’s earnings multiple expanded dramatically. But as growth began to slow, investors believed those hypergrowth days were behind it and the most attractive part of the story was over. As a result, AAPL’s multiple compressed to roughly 12x forward earnings in 2012. What investors missed was that hardware can become a business with annuity characteristics if a company maintains a sustainable edge. Despite a brutal smartphone market, Apple showed it could maintain pricing power, retain customers, and generate recurring revenue through predictable hardware upgrades. Eventually, investors realized Apple didn’t need iPhone growth above 20% to be exceptional. Steady sleep well at night revenue growth of 5 to 10% and earnings growth of 10 to 15% proved hugely valuable, helping the multiple climb from roughly 12 times in 2012 to about 34x calendar 2027 earnings today. Back to NVDA. The question isn’t just how long the current boom lasts, but whether the company can prove durable pricing power and a recurring upgrade cycle for its GPUs. Those massive data centers being built today will need upgrading starting in five years. If Nvidia keeps its edge and captures those upgrades, even with 10 to 15% earnings growth, you can make a case for a higher multiple. The lesson from Apple is that valuation multiples don’t always peak when growth does. Sometimes the biggest expansion comes when investors can sleep well at night given durability and predictability become clear.

items.title: $PENG × $MRVL: 16 TB of DDR5, 576 GB of HBM3E and 57.6 Tbps of bandwidth. This is exactly the direction I've been talking about for months. Penguin just unveiled its MemoryAI Photo
items.body: $PENG × $MRVL: 16 TB of DDR5, 576 GB of HBM3E and 57.6 Tbps of bandwidth. This is exactly the direction I've been talking about for months. Penguin just unveiled its MemoryAI Photonic Appliance, powered by Marvell's Photonic Fabric. The interesting part isn't simply adding more memory. It's making HBM and DDR5 accessible across multiple GPUs and CPUs, potentially across racks. Three memory access modes, including HBM-DDR5 caching, could allow operators to keep latency-sensitive data close to compute while moving capacity-heavy workloads into shared memory. The real opportunity is reducing the amount of expensive HBM required per unit of inference throughput, not replacing HBM. If this architecture delivers competitive latency and bandwidth under real workloads, it could materially improve GPU utilization and cost per token. Sampling starts H2 2027. The specifications are ambitious, but real-world performance will determine whether this becomes a meaningful shift in AI infrastructure economics.

items.title: AI demand is giving suppliers more pricing power in everyday circuit-board materials. At Ventec (6672 TT), general-material prices have nearly doubled this year, while that busines
items.body: AI demand is giving suppliers more pricing power in everyday circuit-board materials. At Ventec (6672 TT), general-material prices have nearly doubled this year, while that business’s gross margin rose from roughly 16–17% in Q1 to about 40% in Q3, according to a Nov. 16 CTBC Securities report. Ventec makes copper-clad laminates and prepregs, the materials used to build and bond the layers of printed circuit boards. The report describes pressure at two levels. Glass-fabric capacity is shifting toward higher-end grades, squeezing the supply of conventional E-glass. Major laminate makers are also prioritizing AI orders, leaving less capacity for lower-end products. Ventec has been taking spillover orders while keeping lead times at about four weeks. Higher prices helped lift margins, alongside a growing share of higher-margin prepregs and more heat-resistant, halogen-free materials. We see this as a way AI spending can raise costs beyond the AI hardware itself. Buyers of conventional board materials can face tighter supply even without stronger demand for their own products. Suppliers that can still deliver gain room to raise prices. That pricing power depends on how long the shortages last. CTBC already sees price increases slowing for thick glass fabric, which can be made on Chinese weaving equipment. The report says Ventec expects supply and demand for thick fabric to improve after Q2 2027.

items.title: Jensen basically built a crazy powerful flywheel on pure conviction and energy. 1. Push the supply chain to move insanely fast, with investments and whatever else it took. 2. Creat
items.body: Jensen basically built a crazy powerful flywheel on pure conviction and energy. 1. Push the supply chain to move insanely fast, with investments and whatever else it took. 2. Create hardware demand by going all in on neoclouds and backing them, pulling future demand forward. 3. Make AI way cheaper. The first two made token prices collapse, and that's why AI adoption took off so fast. 4. Then go hard on every kind of AI app, investing in both digital AI and physical AI. It's like he hit 3x speed on the whole AI industry. And the interesting part is, if you got on board with AI, you pretty much didn't lose. - The AI supply chain and CSPs - Companies using AI to create value - Employees and anyone who's good at using AI So who's losing? Supply chains that couldn't get into AI, because parts and labor got pricier and consumer electronics got wrecked. Companies not using AI, because they'll fall behind. And regular people, who end up with more work or get laid off. So what if that 3x gets turned down to 2x or 1.5x? Keep an eye on those four wheels. Here's another way to look at it. You'd think slower tech progress is bad for the leaders and good for the No. 2 suppliers. But if it slows down a lot, the leaders and the No. 2s end up fighting over the same turf. If that turns into a price war that slows growth across the board, everyone gets hurt. When tech was moving fast, the No. 2s could see their stocks rip just on the dream of breaking in someday. That free ride might be over. So honestly, I'd rather this not happen. But if it does, be ready. I'm not picking a side yet. Investing is just adjusting to the odds as things play out.

items.body: Taipei 101 is lit up tonight with “Taiwan ♡ Jensen.” Less than a week after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, a group of Taiwan tech industry associations pooled their money to pay for the light show. The tower is rotating through “Thrive Together,” and a line about building the future of AI together. For a lot of people here in Taiwan, Jensen never felt like a foreign CEO. He was born in Tainan, he’s at Computex every year, and he’s famous for night market runs and big dinners with his Taiwanese suppliers. Nvidia orders keep a huge part of the island’s supply chain busy, from TSMC to the server makers. The organizers say tonight is about years of working together and hoping that partnership continues.

items.title: Sites with secured power are an enormous asset for $IREN . The more I investigate $NBIS Vineland project, the more I appreciate this advantage. Environmental approvals, regulatory
items.body: Sites with secured power are an enormous asset for $IREN . The more I investigate $NBIS Vineland project, the more I appreciate this advantage. Environmental approvals, regulatory uncertainty, lawsuits, constant disputes. It's a nightmare, and it's already contributed to delays. I'm also investigating $NBIS Birmingham site that relies on grid power, and the picture looks dramatically better. I increasingly believe that grid-connected projects have a much better chance of being delivered on schedule. Once power capacity and the necessary approvals are secured, there are simply fewer opportunities for third parties to disrupt the project. BTM power sounds great on paper. Faster deployment, less dependence on the grid, more control. But the regulatory framework hasn't fully caught up with this model. That leaves plenty of room for legal challenges, conflicting interpretations, and disputes. Even when those challenges ultimately fail, they can still consume time, money, and management attention. And in AI infrastructure, delays are incredibly expensive. I'm starting to think the market may be underestimating just how valuable secured, grid-connected power really is.
