external_articles.title: 5th CSN Greece ICT Conference – Cyprus Shipping Events
external_articles.body:
The 5th CSN Greece ICT Conference, titled “Intelligent Skies, Secure Seas: The AI Impact on ICT”, will take place on 19th November 2026 at the Ploes Floating Venue in Athens.

The conference is placed under the auspices of AMMITEC and supported by the Hellenic Chamber of Shipping , the Propeller Club , HELMEPA , WIMA , Business Events Calendar and MASO Strategic .

Attendance is free of charge for all members of the supporting organisations. However, attendees are encouraged to contribute to the charity foundation supported by the conference , with the option to donate indicated during registration.

Join us to navigate the crossroads of innovation and security and to chart a smarter, safer course for maritime’s digital evolution.

Registration and Welcome Coffee Sponsored by MARPOINT

Note from the organiser Adonis Violaris, Managing Director – CSN

Welcome Address from the Chairman of the Conference Dr. Matthew Maheras, President, AMMITEC, and Chief Information Officer, Metrostar Management Corp.

Keynote Speech Demetris Skourides, Chairman – Research Innovation Foundation Cyprus

We are well past the days of treating ship-to-shore connectivity as a luxury; today’s vessel is an “always-on” operational node. In this session, we will tackle the bandwidth battles head-on, examining how the convergence of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations and maritime 5G is fundamentally altering fleet management.

However, we need to separate what is actually working at sea from what looks good in a brochure. To achieve this, the session will feature our MythBusters format. We have all sat through enough polished sales presentations—this rapid-fire debate will strip away the marketing hype to establish the technical reality of modern satellite communications. We will focus purely on what delivers tangible ROI, what ensures reliable redundancy, and what is merely industry noise.

Setting the Scene: Connectivity as an Operational Reality Dimitris Pavlides, IT Manager – Stealth Maritime

Panel discussion: “MythBusters: SatComs Reality Check”

Moderator: Dimitris Pavlides, IT Manager – Stealth Maritime

Panelists: – Apostolos Giannetsos, ICT Manager – Cyprus Sea Lines – Nikolas Sarantos, ICT Manager – Seahawk Group – Thanos Servos, IT Manager – Seaven – Yiannis Sofianidis, IT Director/CISO – AM Nomikos TWMA SA. – Ilias Vlachogiannis, Head of Fleet ICT – Minerva Marine Inc.

For too long, the maritime sector has treated cybersecurity as a mere compliance exercise. With ships now operating as highly connected, floating data centres, a tick-box approach is no longer fit for purpose. This session focuses on the necessary shift from basic compliance to real-time, dynamic resilience, exploring how we can build robust “human firewall” strategies from the boardroom to the engine room.

To drive this home, we are moving away from the standard slide decks on malware and introducing The War Room . This is a live, audience-driven cyber-attack simulation on a vessel at sea. We will put attendees in the hot seat, forcing them to make critical operational and commercial decisions under pressure. It is designed to stress-test our collective incident response and show exactly what happens when the screens go dark.

Securing the Connected Ecosystem Fotis Tsitsirigkos , Maritime Technology Advisor – FTTCS

Panel discussion: “The War Room: Live Cyber-Attack Simulation on a Vessel”

Moderator: Fotis Tsitsirigkos , Maritime Technology Advisor – FTTCS

Panelists: – Dimitris Perdikaris, Company Security Officer / DPA – Plutofylax Shipping – Manolis Papadakis, CIO/CISO – Dynagas – Ioannis Pantazopoulos, Regional Manager Greece, Cyprus and Turkey – Division Air France, KLM and Delta Air Lines – Demetris Skourides, Chairman – Research Innovation Foundation Cyprus – Kyriakos Mahos, HSQE Director, DPA & CSO – Levante Ferries

AI is actively moving from a conceptual talking point to an operational tool, redefining route optimisation, predictive maintenance, and threat detection. Yet, the introduction of machine intelligence inevitably creates friction with traditional human maritime expertise. We need to understand the new synergy required between the algorithm and the crew.

We will confront these complex dynamics directly through The AI Courtroom . This mock trial will tackle the difficult questions that most panels avoid: the ethics, commercial liability, and legal reality of autonomous and AI-assisted technology. If an AI-optimised system recommends a route that results in an incident, where does the liability lie? Is the industry truly ready to let the algorithm take the wheel?

The Synergy and Friction Between Human and Machine Intelligence Konstantinos Bachxevanis, Solicitor E&W/ Piraeus Bar Lawyer/ Master Mariner – BAX LAW

Panel discussion: “The AI Courtroom: A Mock Trial”

Moderator: Konstantinos Bachxevanis, Solicitor E&W/ Piraeus Bar Lawyer/ Master Mariner – BAX LAW

Panelists: – Konstantinos Stais, Head of ICT & Security – Delia Tankers – Capt. Athanasios Skiadas, Safety Manager/DPA/CSO – Calypso Marine – Capt.George Papanelopoulos, Head of Vetting, Training & Development Dept. – Cyprus Sea Lines Co Ltd – John N. Faraclas, Co-Founder – All About Shipping – George Karistinos, Business Development Manager – ABS Wavesight

This conference is curated for Maritime C-Suite, CIOs, CISOs, Fleet Managers, and Technical Superintendents. If you need to understand the ROI of connectivity, manage the liability of cyber risks, and future-proof your fleet against digital obsolescence, this is your arena.

items.title: Floor & Decor: Still Waiting
items.body: Note: Review all prior FND research and trades on the TSOH website. From “ Floor & Decor: Awaiting Normalization ” (March 2026): “I do not have a great deal of confidence on how or when we get there, but I’m willing to bet on eventual normalization of existing U.S. home sales at the right price - and the ~40% stock price decline over the past 24 months has helped. At less than $55 per share, I think FND would provide a sufficient margin of safety relative to normalized earnings, specifically providing investors with some cover on the number of years needed to return to higher levels of existing U.S. home sales; as a result, I’m a likely buyer if Floor & Decor shares trade down to that level.” [When “ Floor & Decor: Awaiting Normalization ” was published on 03/02/26, FND traded at ~$67 per share.] It continues to be a very challenging environment for flooring retailers like Floor & Decor, as evidenced by the following statistic: they’ve reported twenty consecutive quarters of comp transaction declines, with their average unit volumes declining by ~25% over that period, to levels first eclipsed in FY17. On the Q3 FY26 call, management painted an encouraging picture about the short-term comp trajectory, with improvement in each month throughout the quarter culminating in slight gains in September – the first month of SSS growth at Floor & Decor since January . But they then revealed this had proved short-lived: “Demand for big-ticket discretionary home improvement projects remains challenged, and 30-year mortgage rates are now solidly above 7% - about 115 basis points higher than a year ago – which continues to pressure housing affordability, pending home sales, and existing home sales. In addition, consumers remain selective with larger discretionary purchases, while higher energy costs continue to weigh on sentiment and budgets… As a result, quarter-to-date SSS have declined ~3.8% .” Read more

items.body: 美银最新一期FlowShow很值得看看，Hartnett对市场的态度还是很谨慎，为什么他继续坚持Risk-off，什么条件下才会重新转向Risk-on？这也是理解未来几周美股走势的关键。这份报告最值得关注的有几个方面： 1）全球股票基金单周流入983亿美元，究竟是谁在买？ 2）美国科技股遭遇大规模抛售，为什么全球科技基金仍然持续吸金？ 3）美元、原油、美债收益率和全球流动性之间，正在发生什么变化？ 4）标普500的8000点和7000点情景，背后分别对应什么样的市场结构？ 聊聊Hartnett这期报告聊的几个要点 1、美元成"破坏之球"，全球流动性全面收缩 他的逻辑简明直接：美元飙升加上黄金跌破4000美元，等同于全球流动性的撤退信号。 2、Hartnett为转向风险偏好设定了三个前提条件：油价（WTI）跌破70美元、10年期美债收益率降至4.5%以下、美元开始下行。周五收盘时，三项条件无一达标。 他的逻辑是油价影响通胀、 10年美债收益率决定贴现率和融资成本、美元走强会增加新兴市场的融资压力。 3、而关于资金流向 这里其实有一个分化，前四周被动工具的买入规模约3171亿美元，而主动基金存在较大赎回压力。这背后有一个重要的点： 市场上涨究竟是主动投资者重新看好基本面，还是被动资金、ETF和长期配置资金持续买入的结果？ 两者对市场的意义是不同的： 1）主动投资者推动，意味着风险偏好回归和盈利预期有更强共识。 2）而只是被动资金推动，意味着风险偏好和盈利预期并没有形成共识，这种情况容易出现指数上涨、个股分化、行业内部集中度上升的情况。一旦ETF资金流入放缓，市场的边际买盘就可能迅速减弱。 4、Hartnett 对未来市场的另一个判断：投资者情绪悲观，但实际仓位并没有那么悲观。 Hartnett 特别提到即将公布的11月17日美银全球基金经理调查需要重点关注三个指标：繁荣预期、现金仓位、实际股票仓位。 如果现金仓位上升至4.2%以上，说明基金经理开始真正降低风险资产配置。这反而可能改善市场情绪指标，减少之前的拥挤交易风险。 这里有一个潜在的风险： 同一天美银经济团队认为，通胀持续高于2%目标，可能迫使美联储重新考虑此前的宽松路径，甚至需要进一步提高利率。 同时，该团队也承认如果经济明显放缓、美国与伊朗达成协议导致油价回落，或者股票市场大幅下跌，后续加息可能推迟甚至取消。 把本期Hartnett报告与近期看到的的机构资金流、AI融资、美国财政和美联储政策结合起来，我的判断是： 市场可能已经完成一轮仓位清洗，但宏观压力和流动性风险尚未解除 1）短期：市场有反弹条件，但不能简单理解为新一轮牛市已经开始 对冲基金已经大幅降低杠杆，部分拥挤交易被清理。长期基金却仍在持续买入股票。 这意味着市场下跌时的边际卖盘可能减少，出现空头回补和逢低买入推动的反弹。但反弹是否能够持续，需要观察主动基金是否重新增加风险敞口。 2）中期 最大的风险来自宏观金融条件与AI政策及融资态势的碰撞 我认为目前最值得警惕的组合是：油价长期维持高位、美元继续走强、美债收益率居高不下、科技公司债券发行增加且融资成本进一步上升。 这些因素同时发生，就可能出现AI产业需求仍然旺盛，但资本市场对投资回报率的审视和挑剔更高，这会导致科技产业内部出现更加明显的分化。 拥有强大现金流、资产负债表和商业化能力的公司，会比依赖外部融资的公司更有优势。 所以未来核心是看中期宏观环境的变化，个人角度就聚焦就看三个层面： 1）油价/通胀的走势； 2）中期选举新政治生态下AI政策确实是进一步收紧还只是纠偏； 3）AI商业化是不是还处于加速状态（大云厂的云业务增速和模型厂的实际营收增速）。

items.body: 只有用过电子支付，才知道有多方便。 很多人一旦习惯了这种支付方式，基本就再也回不去了。但现在加密世界和 Web2 之间依然存在一道壁垒。稳定币虽然方便，但真正到了日常生活中，很多消费场景还是不能直接使用。想把钱转出来，又要面对各种出金渠道、手续费以及合规风险。 说白了，链上有钱是一回事，能不能方便、安全地花出去又是另一回事。而 @EthenaPay 想解决的，恰恰就是这个问题。而且 Ethena Pay 最近又进行了一个挺实用的更新：支持通过用户名轻松转账！ 以后给别人转账，不用再复制一长串钱包地址，也不用反复核对那些复杂的字符，直接输入对方的 Ethena Pay 用户名，就能完成转账。这看起来只是一个小功能，但实际上是在降低 Web3 支付的使用门槛。 我一直觉得，稳定币真正的价值不应该只体现在交易所里交易、在 DeFi 里挖矿，而是能够像我们平时使用电子支付一样，真正融入日常生活。 未来 Ethena Pay 正式在中国上线后，预计将按照 Waitlist（候补名单）的顺序逐步开放用户注册和使用。完成注册并成功开通后，用户也将有机会分享自己的推荐码。因此，提前加入 Waitlist，或许能在未来开放时抢占先机！ https://t.co/IUZAUlLk7C 我觉得加密支付真正的终点，不应该是让所有人都学会使用区块链，而是让普通人根本感觉不到区块链的存在。

items.title: Liquid-cooling connector demand is already filling production lines at Lotes (3533 TT), which aims to double quick-disconnect capacity over the coming quarter. We see that as a use
items.body: Liquid-cooling connector demand is already filling production lines at Lotes (3533 TT), which aims to double quick-disconnect capacity over the coming quarter. We see that as a useful signal for investors following the pace of liquid-cooling adoption. Lotes, a Taiwanese supplier of CPU sockets and connectors, reported full utilization of its quick-disconnect (QD) lines in notes from its Nov. 13 earnings call. These fittings connect coolant lines and allow them to be disconnected for servicing. QDs accounted for about 1% of Lotes’ revenue in July and 2% in August. The company expects that share to reach 3–5% in December and close to 10% for full-year 2027. For Vertiv a component supplier running flat out adds evidence of demand further down the supply chain. For Amphenol, Lotes’ expansion raises a question about how much of that growth comes from a larger market and how much comes from suppliers winning share. Lotes also offers a view into the next server CPU upgrade cycle. The call notes put a faster ramp for AMD’s Venice platform around the end of Q1 2027. Intel’s Oak Stream has slipped from an earlier expectation of H2 2026 to initial small-volume shipments around late Q1 or early Q2 2027, with a more substantial ramp in H2. Those timings matter for when demand for the new CPU sockets builds. From Lotes’ perspective, Venice starts accelerating around the end of Q1, while Oak Stream’s larger contribution comes later in the year. $VRT $APH $AMD $INTC

items.title: Singapore-listed Geo Energy Resources stock traded down 23% this morning before the company filed for a trading halt Reason? Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said over the wee
items.body: Singapore-listed Geo Energy Resources stock traded down 23% this morning before the company filed for a trading halt Reason? Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said over the weekend that at least 70% of the proceeds from the management of all local mining permits should go to the state. If necessary, the state should hold controlling stakes in these mining assets This is hard-line resource nationalism policy Recall that Indonesia was the one who pioneered the Production Sharing Contract (PSC) for the oil & gas sector. One may argue on indigenous principles that the state should retain ownership of all natural resources in the country; in the case of O&G, despite the PSC arrangement, foreign oil majors still chose to participate and assumed all risks/costs related to exploration and development, with proceeds from production split with the state But this comes as a time when foreign investors are getting jittery about governance Fun fact: Jim Rogers (the legendary commod investor) used to be a backer of Geo Energy Resources. He retired from the board in 2023 and had divested (most of) his holdings

items.title: Introducing 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝: https://t.co/YaLEMbmKwf. A hermetic, pixel-perfect X post renderer in safe Rust / wasm. Zero browser, network, filesystem, system fonts. Renders a post to PNG in
items.body: Introducing 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝: https://t.co/YaLEMbmKwf. A hermetic, pixel-perfect X post renderer in safe Rust / wasm. Zero browser, network, filesystem, system fonts. Renders a post to PNG in ~1ms (and 0.4 ms for @jack's "setting up my twttr" 😁). X is the global town square, and the medium is the message. Being able to preview what things will look like before posting is great for both humans and agents. Rendering with xeet is is 100x-1000x faster than booting up a browser and taking a screenshot, yet it's just as accurate. It reproduces Blink & HarfBuzz text shaping, 1/64px line breaking, RTL bidi, 28 Chirp font subsets, CJK/Math/Emoji fallbacks, "Show more" rules, etc. It's the kind of thing that would be wildly impractical, if not impossible, for a human engineer to pull off. Except 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝 is structured as an "autorepo." An oracle boots up Chrome, and verifies tens of thousands of text layout rules. A CI canary then watches the evolution of the original, and files signed PRs for agents to act on. It was conceived from the ground up around 'verification engineering', and the result speaks for itself. Enjoy!

items.body: 对我而言，我觉得现在就是加密行业最黑暗的时刻。 而且我认为，这种变化很大程度上是合规化带来的，尤其是 ETF。ETF 的出现，确实给 bitcoin:native 带来了大量传统金融资金，短期内也为价格提供了支撑。但问题是，BTC 最初最有魅力的东西，恰恰不是它能吸引多少华尔街资金，而是它代表的自由。 一个不需要银行、不需要政府许可、不依赖任何中心化机构的金融体系。但现在呢？BTC 越来越像美国传统金融体系的一部分。华尔街掌握着越来越多的定价权，机构资金决定着市场情绪，监管政策影响着行业走向。曾经那个试图打破旧金融秩序的东西，正在被旧金融秩序一点点吸收。 这并不是说 ETF 本身不好，也不是说机构资金不重要。问题在于，当整个行业都开始围绕合规、机构、监管和传统资本转动时，我们是不是正在丢掉最初进入这个行业的理由？ 另外，我对 BTC 未来的悲观，还有一个很重要的原因：美国政治周期。 特朗普上台之后，一直把自己包装成加密行业最友好的总统。无论是推动美国成为加密中心，还是支持 BTC 战略储备，都给市场带来了不少想象空间。但这里面有一个问题：特朗普的支持，到底有多少是真正为了推动加密行业发展，又有多少是政治利益和个人商业利益的结合？ solana:6p6xgHyF7AeE6TZkSmFsko444wqoP15icUSqi2jfGiPN ethereum:0xda5e1988097297dcdc1f90d4dfe7909e847cbef6 这些项目，让特朗普家族在加密市场获得了巨大的商业曝光和利益。可反过来看，除了给市场带来短期情绪和政策预期，他究竟给加密行业留下了多少真正能够长期延续的制度性改变？ 我比较担心的是，随着特朗普政治影响力发生变化，尤其是2029年任期结束之后，民主党重新掌握政策主导权后会对特朗普任内的加密政策，相关项目以及利益关系，都可能成为新的政治审查对象。 这里面最麻烦的地方在于，加密可能不再只是一个金融和技术问题，而是被卷入美国两党的政治斗争。如果民主党把特朗普时期的加密政策视为政治遗产，甚至将其作为清算对象，那么整个行业都可能受到波及。 所以我觉得，加密行业正在经历一个历史上很尴尬的转变：以前我们担心的是技术能不能实现、生态能不能发展、用户能不能进来。现在我们却要关心美国总统是谁，国会由谁控制，下一届政府会不会推翻上一届的政策。 一个号称去中心化、无需许可的行业，最后却要看美国政府的脸色吃饭，这本身就是一种讽刺。 我并不是看空 BTC 的技术，也不是认为它会归零。我只是觉得，当 BTC 越来越依赖传统金融机构和美国政治环境时，它原本最核心的价值主张，正在面临一场真正的考验。

items.body: One of my favorite results of all time is Sinkhorn's - dating to just 1963. Sinkhorn balancing is an iterative procedure that turns a non-negative matrix into a doubly stochastic matrix by iteratively normalizing its rows, then columns. It's amazing that it works at all - a small miracle that makes many things possible: It solves optimal transport problems, it's at the core of the PageRank algorithm, it's used in SLAM, in multi-omics alignment, supply chain routing, market design, and more

items.body: https://t.co/CYB0vLZOxi TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10AM TO 10PM on 11/15/26 In this window the succession fight split in public on the same Sunday shows that moved the congressional track. Jensen Huang has agreed to a closed-door interview with the three House committees, with no subpoena needed and the date still being discussed. A briefed Gang of Eight member said on the record that the intelligence community does not know whether Alice Huang was a witting asset. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent directed the board toward an outside chief executive and set it a 10-day deadline to answer on export-compliance culture, while the Financial Times reported Huang himself is discussing a comeback, with an ally war room lobbying for his return. THE INTERVIEW IS AGREED • House Select Committee on China Chair John Moolenaar said on CBS Face the Nation on Sunday, November 15 that Jensen Huang has agreed to come in for a closed-door interview with the three House committees, Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and the Select Committee on China, and that representatives from Nvidia will also come in. • Asked whether that means no subpoena will be needed and Huang will sit down in the next few weeks, just without a date yet, Moolenaar answered: "That's correct." The committees are in the process of discussing exact dates, so the December 1 date in the chairs' November 12 letter is not locked. • Moolenaar framed the purpose as understanding "to what degree privileged information was accessed" and "to what degree this potential alleged Chinese spy influenced Nvidia's philosophy" and, through it, United States policy on AI and export controls. • This is the first public confirmation by a chair that Huang has accepted the committees' interview request itself. The November 13 written acceptance deadline had passed with no public confirmation, refusal, subpoena issuance, or committee statement in the record. WHAT THE INTELLIGENCE DOES NOT KNOW • Representative Jim Himes, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee and a Gang of Eight member who was briefed on the Nvidia matter in the past week, said on Face the Nation that United States intelligence does not know whether Alice Huang was an asset of Chinese intelligence: "I don't think that we know. I don't think that we know." • Himes said: "It's possible, based on what I know, that Alice Huang had no idea that she was maybe being monitored or working for the Chinese. That's possible. We don't know the answer to that question. It's also possible on the other end of the spectrum that she was a fully paid up intelligence asset and actually communicating." • Himes also said the Rubio memo described in CNN reporting has not been shared with the Gang of Eight, and that the only information that came their way was "a glancing not on the agenda discussion" in that meeting. • In the same broadcast, CBS reported its own reporting, stated by the anchor: two law enforcement sources told CBS that the Justice Department's National Security Division is investigating Megaspeed. There is no Justice Department statement in the record. The existence of a Justice Department Megaspeed probe is already in the record; the National Security Division attribution is the new detail. BESSENT WANTS AN OUTSIDE CEO • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Fox News Sunday Morning Futures on Sunday, November 15, per Reuters reporting of his on-air words: "This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company, that just (with) what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shakeup." • Bessent also set Nvidia's board and its outside counsel a deadline of the next 10 days, by about November 25, to answer questions about the company's culture of compliance with export restrictions: "What was the culture at Nvidia and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings? I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel." • No prior claim in the record has an administration official publicly directing the succession outcome toward an outside chief executive, calling for a dramatic shakeup, or setting the board and outside counsel a 10-day answer deadline on compliance culture. THE COMEBACK REPORT • The Financial Times reported on Sunday, November 15, citing people familiar with the matter, that Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive and has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, days after resigning on November 12. • Per the Financial Times reporting, one Huang ally said they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former chief's return and would try to garner support from the White House, and said: "Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen." The ally said the efforts had Huang's support. • Spokespeople for Nvidia and for Huang declined to comment to the Financial Times, per the reporting. The Financial Times original is paywalled and was not read firsthand in the case record; the report was read through Reuters same-day report of the Financial Times piece and agreeing carriages, and it is carried at that grade. • This is the first reporting that Huang himself is discussing his own return and that an organized ally effort to lobby the board and the White House has his support. It lands the same day as Bessent's public call for an outside chief executive, in the opposite direction. THE CHECKPOINTS • November 17: Nvidia earnings, and the Warren and Coons records preservation confirmation is due. • November 18: the briefing track. • November 24: Bennet's answers due. • About November 25: Bessent's 10-day deadline for answers from Nvidia's board and outside counsel on export-compliance culture. • December 1: Huang's closed-door transcribed interview before the three House committees, date not locked, and the House Foreign Affairs Democrats' answers due. • December 2: Teter's requested closed-door transcribed interview. • December 3: Scott's requested public Senate Banking hearing with Huang, and the Foreign Affairs hearing with Under Secretary Kessler at 10 a.m. • December 10: Scott's requested public Senate Banking hearing with Lutnick.

external_articles.title: Jensengate | Atlas Peak Research
external_articles.body:
The fall of Jensen Huang at Nvidia, tracked in twelve-hour editions: the newest edition in full at the top, and every earlier edition in the archive below.

TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10PM TO 10AM on 11/16/26

In this window the first government act in the case landed. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule closing the remote access channel at the center of the Megaspeed business model, and imposed a new destination license requirement covering Singapore and Malaysia, Megaspeed's two operating jurisdictions. The Straits Times reported the first known enforcement action in Indonesia linked to the case, a police search of Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary that found empty server racks and no chips. President Trump publicly welcomed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive, in the opposite direction from his Treasury secretary's push for an outside chief executive.

In this window the succession fight split in public on the same Sunday shows that moved the congressional track. Jensen Huang has agreed to a closed-door interview with the three House committees, with no subpoena needed and the date still being discussed. A briefed Gang of Eight member said on the record that the intelligence community does not know whether Alice Huang was a witting asset. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent directed the board toward an outside chief executive and set it a 10-day deadline to answer on export-compliance culture, while the Financial Times reported Huang himself is discussing a comeback, with an ally war room lobbying for his return.

In this window the channel record widened again: the Wall Street Journal reported records showing Megaspeed arranged to send nearly $12 billion of top Nvidia chips to companies in China, a fifth chip figure with its own window, and reported an unwritten Nvidia rule capping partners' Chinese customers and a new channel node, Aolani Cloud. Megaspeed answered publicly for the first time on Alice Huang, saying she left the company effective August 30, 2025 and that it has retained outside counsel for an internal investigation. The Washington Post reported Huang is quietly helping pick his own successor, and Elon Musk said many of Nvidia's supply deals were a handshake with Huang personally.

In this window the fight over the classified memo at the center of the case widened: the Washington Post reported the memo was Secretary of State Marco Rubio's recasting of a CIA report in more assertive terms, and CNN reported the CIA is not yet convinced the intercepts prove Alice Huang knowingly funneled information to Beijing. The Financial Times reported Nvidia carries directors and officers insurance that protects its directors personally and not the company, filings show a director sold about $946.6 million of stock in the weeks before the board inquiry opened, and Reuters reported Chinese AI firms are racing to reserve Nvidia powered capacity outside China before the remote rental loophole closes. South Korea said Nvidia has reconfirmed its 260,000 GPU supply plan after the resignation, Bill Ackman defended Huang on presumption of innocence grounds, and the first Sunday show booking for a case chair was announced for tomorrow.

Overnight, Reuters reported that Jensen Huang told Nvidia's own general counsel and chief marketing officer in writing that his interactions with Alice Huang and Megaspeed were standard business dealings, the House chairs' 8 p.m. deadline for his written acceptance of the December 1 interview passed with nothing public, and a filings-based reconstruction put $5,353 million of Nvidia's formerly Singapore-billed revenue with China and Hong Kong headquartered buyers. Super Micro denied on the record that Megaspeed was ever its customer, a sitting administration official argued Huang should have been warned the way a congressman once was, and the street kept repricing the overhang: HSBC cut its target by more than half, and a billionaire holder said he will make no further investment in Nvidia without Huang.

Today the fight over the Megaspeed Entity List delay became an open cabinet split, the Commerce Secretary's own tenure came into question, Reuters documented the scale of Chinese AI projects built around restricted Nvidia chips, and the succession search moved in public for the first time: the board was reported to have approached an external candidate, then issued its first statement calling candidate speculation premature, while two major holders asked the board to slow the process down and keep Jensen Huang's return on the table. The 8 p.m. deadline for Huang's written acceptance of the December 1 interview passed with nothing public.

THE SUCCESSION SEARCH MOVES, THEN THE BOARD PUSHES BACK

Overnight, the House turned its request to Jensen Huang into an ultimatum with a deadline tonight, the Senate Banking subpoena threat was verified from the letter itself and shown to run to Huang only, Bloomberg published the first account of how the admission and the resignation decision actually happened, Malaysia opened its own official inquiry into the Megaspeed channel while its prime minister said there is no indication so far that chips were exported from Malaysia, and CNN's reporting reframed the Alice Huang spy question toward recruitment after access.

The first full day after Jensen Huang's resignation widened the case on every front at once. Huang agreed to testify before Congress, the Senate Banking Committee requested dated public hearings for Huang and for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, the tax committees opened their own investigation with a records preservation demand, the Justice Department spoke on the record for the first time, Singapore published its full account of the Alice Huang investigation, and the channel record added two new end points, DeepSeek and Huawei.

THE TAX COMMITTEES OPEN AN INVESTIGATION

The case resolved overnight. Nvidia announced this morning that Jensen Huang has resigned, effective immediately, ending the board process that had built through the night: Semafor had reported some directors favored CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, and Kress is the interim appointment in the release. The night also deepened the record behind the case, with the Wall Street Journal's account of the husband who introduced Huang to Alice Huang, Congress turning its fire on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Megaspeed's first public statement, and the analyst downgrade wave broadening before the announcement landed.

In twelve hours the case moved from congressional pressure to the boardroom. The New York Times reported a second extramarital relationship, this one with a direct report. The Wall Street Journal reported the board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang, and Bloomberg reported a succession search is under way. The committees' 5 PM deadline for his answer on the November 18 briefing passed with no acceptance or alternative date reported, and the desk raised its exit estimate in this window.

Atlas Peak Research. Compiled from public reporting, company statements, and congressional and court records. Each edition covers twelve hours of the case and appears here in full.

Updated 11/16/26 10:07 AM ET · 10 editions

items.body: 老黄讨论回归，贝森特说英伟达必须从外部寻找CEO。这怎么看？ 1、金融时报说老黄已与亲信讨论了回归的可能性， 他们正在组建一个由硅谷高管组成的“作战室”，以游说支持前英伟达负责人的回归，并将试图争取白宫的支持； 而就在同一时间，财政部长贝森特表态称赞黄仁勋是“了不起的创新者”，英伟达也非常出色。但同时他要求英伟达董事会及外部律师必须在“未来10天内”就公司出口限制合规文化作出答复。 在管理层问题上，他直言英伟达领导层需要“大幅调整”，并建议公司应当寻找外部人士来担任新CEO。此外，他还指出，上级与下属建立恋爱关系是“企业大忌”。 2、只能说支持和反对的声音都很大。以老马为首的一众美国科技大佬，还有英伟达内部大部分员工都是强烈支持老黄，其实英伟达这些机构股东们例如贝莱德、富达、先锋和到富等机构，估计也都希望老黄回归，不然受损都是自己的账户、大部分资本还是求利。估计产业生态大部分伏击也都支持，毕竟很多都是一损俱损。 当然前提条件就是如果要回归：老黄得严格遵守新的芯片出口条例，只能埋头技术发展，别在妄图钻政策空子，同时保持低调甚至避免跟川普的直接沟通。 3、另外一点就是贝森特的表态也说明了共和党内“倒黄”并不是说的就是鲁比奥一人所为，还是之前的观点这是多股力量的合力。 但也意味着回归之路会艰难和坎坷，反对的态度比较坚挺。“倒黄”派既担心老黄回归之后故伎重演，又担心他去影响川普的态度和判断。 这中间的博弈估计是反复多次，还有本周的国会听证会。 这期间英伟达的估计估计会随着老黄能回归和回归希望被打消这个两个状态之间反复，上上次下好几次也很有可能。 最后如果确定老黄真能回归（回归身份最好是CEO、其次是董事会主席、最差得是个顾问），可能才会迎来反转。 本条由@bitget_zh赞助，「Bitget 买美股：秒级入场，丝滑交易

items.title: The US press (and parts of the Admin?) are not doing their job on NVDA and Singapore. OR they have an alternative agenda 🤔. It is fairly easy to find out what a "Singapore sale" to
items.body: The US press (and parts of the Admin?) are not doing their job on NVDA and Singapore. OR they have an alternative agenda 🤔. It is fairly easy to find out what a "Singapore sale" to a large US customer actually looks like. This is all gettable public info… I had agents request filings in Singapore for known subs of the big US buyers. They got some but not all. Then a curious friend passed along the Dell file (h/t @RandianCapital). This of course begs the question of why anyone is pushing this narrative when it's this easy to check. NVDA may well have real questions to answer on China or Megaspeed, but this Singapore angle is likely just not it… So here is one example. Dell's global buying hub is Dell Global B.V. (Singapore Branch). It's a Dutch co w/ a Singapore address and a US parent, also audited by PwC. In the yr ended Jan ‘25 it did $56.6bn of rev (59% of all of Dell), nearly all of it selling to other Dell units, and 55% of that was for the US. By my math it bought about $30.8bn from outside suppliers, up from $20.2bn the year before. The filing says it holds "AI commodities" in inventory, and raw materials doubled. Dell shipped $9.8bn of AI servers that year. If GPUs are ~2/3 ish of the price of an AI server, that's $6-7bn of GPUs. NVDA reported $23.7bn billed to Singapore in the same fiscal year. So **one US customer** could plausibly be about a quarter of the "Singapore" line by itself. I’ll let others go pull the Singapore filings for other large known GPU buyers… To be clear, the filing doesn't name NVDA or any supplier, the GPU share is my estimate, and I don't know who the other billers are. But this is a US company whose Singapore branch buys the parts, holds AI components in inventory and sells most of it on to the US. Under NVDA's old billing location table that is a Singapore sale, the same ones the press say “disappeared”. And thanks to @RandianCapital for the spirited and thoughtful debate. @GavinSBaker @elonmusk @Jason @balajis @TimSweeneyEpic

items.title: CMP pad supplier Praise Victor (7768 TT) told us it is short of capacity and expanding, as chip packaging takes on polishing steps that used to belong mainly to wafer fabs. Its sub
items.body: CMP pad supplier Praise Victor (7768 TT) told us it is short of capacity and expanding, as chip packaging takes on polishing steps that used to belong mainly to wafer fabs. Its subsidiary IV Technologies makes CMP pads, and its customers include $TSM and $MU. Semiconductor products were 66% of revenue in the first half of 2026, up from 48% in 2023. At this month’s NCKU Materials Industry Forum, we are pleased to talk to IV Technologies President Yang Wei Wen. He told us CoWoS lines in Taiwan already use a lot of CMP, and that CoPoS will bring in new materials, including glass substrates in the future. Supply is the constraint here. At its August earnings call, the company said existing lines were close to full and that a major advanced-packaging customer had asked it to hold 90 days of inventory. New plants in Hefei and Taichung are expected to contribute from 2027, and Yang said a new R&D center will be completed next year. Our read: pads are consumables, so demand follows the number of polishing steps as well as the number of wafers. If packaging keeps adding planarization, pad demand rises with packaging capacity too. How quickly Praise Victor benefits depends on when its new plants pass customer qualification. Our full interview with Yang is in the video.

items.title: NVIDIA's sales to Singapore has resurfaced over the past few days, with discourse centering on how much of it is end-customer use versus invoicing/transshipment It's a common pract
items.body: NVIDIA's sales to Singapore has resurfaced over the past few days, with discourse centering on how much of it is end-customer use versus invoicing/transshipment It's a common practice amongst multinational/regional companies to use transfer pricing/profit allocation as part of tax optimization, though the benefits-versus-costs of such has been narrowing with the OECD corporate tax rules (global minimum tax, and reallocation of taxing rights) Singapore has various tax incentives (grants/reliefs), tax treaties, etc, that MNCs consider favorable when deciding where to set up their APAC HQ/booking center. Obviously, the entities being set up need to have economic substance (rather than shells) - and it helps with Singapore's stable political and regulatory regime, talent pool, public infrastructure for companies to establish active ops there Many global tech companies - including those in the semiconductor supply chain - have done so An example - Apple. They have entities set up in Singapore and their largest subsidiary in Singapore is a regional sales & marketing hub They booked close to $40B of pre-tax profits in their Singapore subsidiaries in 2025, which could rise up to $50B this year (based on FT estimates) Their effective tax rate in Singapore has fluctuated around 10% between 2023-2025 due to certain tax reliefs/incentives, but this is expected to normalize to close to 15%, with claw-back through top-up taxes to align with OECD tax rules Back to NVIDIA - Their sales to Singapore peaked at 22% of total revenues in FQ2/25 ($10.2B) from ~8% in FY23 What is clear, based on Singspore's trade ministry's statement, is that physical delivery of products sold by NVIDIA to Singapore represents less than 1% of NVIDIA's overall revenues. These products are mainly deployed in Singapore for major enterprises and the Singapore government As for the balance, it remains unclear how much and where the physical shipments end up, and how much of the billings are profit-shifting. This is the critical point that needs to be addressed tl;dr - there are nuances to what news headlines suggest about Singapore being used as a tax shelter or transshipment hub

items.title: NVIDIA Lost Its Founder. Anthropic IPOs This Week. What Happens to the AI Infra Trade Now?
items.body: Jensen Huang is out. Anthropic is pricing a roughly $1 trillion IPO this week while turning its own suppliers into shareholders. Sam Altman is telling Samsung the constraints are physical. Michael Dell just showed an H100 that was supposed to be obsolete renting for 58% more than a year ago. None of this is noise, but it’s the opposite of the slowdown everyone is pricing in. The person left. The platform did not. NVIDIA closed around $163 on November 13, roughly 32% off the October peak near $239–243 and below $4 trillion for the first time since mid-2025. The board accepted/forced Huang’s resignation effective immediately after the dual-affair revelations. Colette Kress is interim CEO. Harvey Jones is the first board chair. Rene Haas has already been approached. This is a real governance event. Huang ran a flat organization with roughly 60 direct reports and no formal succession plan . The WSJ reported he belittled the finance team over guarantees tied to deals involving his son-in-law that financed upstart cloud and data-center developers. The large institutional financing complex that used NVIDIA chips as collateral now has a succession question attached to it. That is the risk premium the market is currently charging. It is not a fundamental change to the product roadmap, the CUDA moat, the supply chain, or customer demand. Ian Buck remains the internal technical anchor . External options with culture fit exist. The company reports Q3 on November 17 with a ~$108 billion guide and still-accelerating data-center growth. The AI infra supercycle does not pause because of board politics or a personal investigation. Subscribe now Anthropic aligned the entire stack with skin in the game. The S-1 and the roadshow paint a clear picture here. October ARR hit $81 billion. The Q4’26 guide of roughly $19.3 billion annualizes lower only because of holiday seasonality , the deliberate removal of distillation revenue , and Opus 5.5 pricing about 40% cheaper on a like-for-like basis. There is no Meta or Microsoft pullback. Training and R&D compute is modeled at roughly $90 billion in 2027 and rises sharply thereafter. Management is deliberately over-ordering capacity so they never hit another SpaceX-style crunch. Cash burn worsens next year on purpose . Goldman is modeling more than $600 billion in revenue by 2030 and the company has already committed roughly $900 billion to computing capacity. IMO, more important than the numbers is the structure. A concurrent $26 billion private placement at the IPO price is being taken by the suppliers themselves: Pricing at $70–78 implies roughly $917 billion to $1.02 trillion on outstanding shares (up to about $1.4 trillion fully diluted). Net proceeds to Anthropic are more than $85 billion that go straight into more compute . The companies that sell the GPUs, HBM, networking, and wafers just bought equity in their largest customer. As an AI Infrastructure investor, I understand this as a very well aligned multi-year demand visibility. Subscribe now Altman and Dell confirmed the physical constraints. Altman told Samsung executives the usual rules of a commodity business do not apply, demand will grow enormously over the long term, and the biggest constraints over the next few years are the chip supply chain and data-center infrastructure. Token demand is structural. He also flagged short-term double-counting around neoclouds and noted that only OpenAI and Anthropic are currently driving the major growth. The binding constraints remain physical . Dell made it tangible. The company started shipping H100s in 2022. A year ago the rental rate was $1.96 per hour. Today it is $3.10 — a 58% increase on a chip that was supposed to be obsolete. So much for GPU depreciation. Scarcity is real and pricing power is still rising on older silicon while the industry races to Blackwell and Vera Rubin. Valuations have already done the hard work. From late June to early November, semiconductor forward earnings estimates rose about 30% while the forward multiple compressed about 35% . AI infrastructure as a group showed nearly identical dynamics. Memory multiples were cut in half while estimates rose. NVIDIA itself now trades at roughly 10× forward earnings depending on the exact window. This sits among the cheapest levels in more than a decade relative to its own growth, and at a discount to the broader market and to most other AI giants. The market is wrongly pricing AI infrastructure as if the demand is cyclical and the leadership vacuum is permanent. The actual data shows multi-year, non-cancellable capacity commitments, supplier equity alignment, rising rental rates on “obsolete” hardware, and deliberate over-ordering to avoid future crunches. Is this a good moment to be bullish? Yes. The mega-correction has removed a large part of the speculative premium. The remaining risk is real: succession execution, power and permitting delays after the midterms, potential short-term utilization softness from over-ordering, and the usual circularity concerns. But the asymmetric setup has improved : the structural demand lock-in is clearer than it was at the peak, the valuations feel quite cheap, and the bottlenecks continue to capture every incremental dollar of the $90 billion-plus training spend and the multi-hundred-billion commitments. The AI infra trade is wrongly being re-priced lower. When the market finally prices the structural reality instead of the person and the short-term narrative, the re-rating in the real choke points will be violent and aggresive. Stay long the picks and shovels. The future is still extremely bright. The Founder, Outlier Capital Not financial advice. Do your own work.

items.title: $NVDA NVIDIA EARNINGS, TUESDAY NOVEMBER 17: THE COMPLETE DILIGENCE LIST THE SETUP Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 after the close on Tuesday, November 17. The quarter ended October 25. Gu
items.body: $NVDA NVIDIA EARNINGS, TUESDAY NOVEMBER 17: THE COMPLETE DILIGENCE LIST THE SETUP Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 after the close on Tuesday, November 17. The quarter ended October 25. Guidance is revenue of $108 billion plus or minus 2 percent, gross margin 74 percent plus or minus 50 basis points. Consensus sits at $109.0 billion for revenue and $2.47 for adjusted earnings per share, and it has barely moved in four weeks. The street has not cut this quarter for the governance crisis. The numbers it expects are the numbers the old regime promised. This is also the first print of the post-Jensen era. Colette Kress runs the call as interim CEO and CFO. The numbers matter. The language matters more. Here is everything worth monitoring, in the order it will arrive. THE NUMBERS, FIRST 10 MINUTES - Revenue against the $108 billion guide and the $109.0 billion consensus. A print inside the guide band but below consensus is a miss wearing a beat's clothes. Score it as a miss. - Data center revenue against $101.8 billion of consensus, and inside it compute against $80.7 billion and networking against $20.0 billion. Networking strong with compute light is mix shift toward systems. Both light is a demand problem. - The segment cuts by customer type: hyperscale at $53.3 billion of consensus, AI clouds and industrial at $48.9 billion, edge computing at $7.5 billion. The AI clouds line is the neocloud bucket. Its beat or miss is the cleanest read on the demand quality of the ecosystem Nvidia finances. - Gross margin against the 74 percent guide and 74.1 percent consensus. Last quarter guided the fiscal Q4 margin down to a 71 to 72 percent trough, partly on memory costs. Slippage now means the trough arrives early or deeper. - Operating discipline: consensus expects $72.1 billion of adjusted operating income on $9.0 billion of operating expense. In a transition quarter, expense discipline is the first place a careful CFO shows her hand. - Everything outside data center is only about $7 billion of the $109 billion. Gaming, visualization, and autos cannot save a data center miss or sink a data center beat. Note them and move on. - Free cash flow against roughly $59 billion of consensus, and the quarter's buyback total. Acceleration reads as management buying its own transition discount. Deceleration reads as conservation ahead of the commitment stack. - Inventory, receivables, and days sales outstanding. In a quarter defined by a diversion scandal running through intermediaries, receivables growing faster than revenue is the first number skeptics will reach for. - Operating cash flow against net income. The quality test that has flagged lesser names all season. THE GUIDE The Q4 guide is the only forward number that matters Tuesday night. Consensus for Q4 already sits at $124.7 billion of revenue, with the margin trough of about 71.9 percent built in. The lowest published model, already cut once for export restriction risk, is $120 billion. A guide that reaches only the low model is a consensus miss of nearly $5 billion, and it will be traded as one. More important than the guide itself is one sentence from last quarter. On the August call, management guided preliminary fiscal 2028 revenue growth of approximately 70 percent year over year, supply constrained. Reaffirmed, qualified, or silently dropped are three different stocks. That sentence gets compared word by word against the August transcript. Watch also for any new caveat vocabulary that was not there in August: visibility, prudence, transition. New words in a guidance paragraph are a downgrade in plain sight. PRODUCT AND SUPPLY - Vera Rubin was guided to about 20 percent of Q3 data center revenue. Above or below that line grades the ramp. - Supply and capacity commitments went from $119 billion to $279 billion in a single quarter, mostly memory procurement. The new 10-Q figure is a same-night check. Another step up of that size is demand conviction and balance sheet commitment in the same number. - Memory pricing. Management's own flagged line last quarter was that the magnitude of the price increase had exceeded expectations. Whether HBM costs are still escalating, now locked, or passing through to prices decides the margin path into 2027. - Any cancellation, pushout, or double-ordering language, anywhere on the call. CHINA AND EXPORT CONTROLS The standing line is no China data center compute revenue in the outlook. Unchanged, loosened, or tightened all trade differently. Nobody will say the words Megaspeed or diversion. Listen instead for the euphemisms: certain customers, enhanced know-your-customer, end-use verification, new compliance costs. And in the 10-Q, watch the revenue geography note. Last quarter's filing reclassified $20.6 billion of Singapore-billed revenue by buyer headquarters, $5.35 billion of it to China and Hong Kong. Whether that presentation extends or quietly disappears is a disclosure decision, and it will be read as one. If an analyst forces a revenue-at-risk number for the export bills now moving in Congress, whether management quantifies or refuses is itself the tell. THE ECOSYSTEM BALANCE SHEET Nvidia is the AI ecosystem's underwriter as well as its supplier, and the call is a chance to see whether that changes. The stack to re-read in the new 10-Q: $279 billion of supply commitments, $36 billion of AI cloud purchase agreements, $108.5 billion of maximum guarantee exposure including $105 billion of residual value guarantees behind a single Ohio campus leased to OpenAI, about $164.5 billion of total customer support against $229 billion of shareholders' equity. Listen for whether the August financing platforms with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR get mentioned at all, and in what tense: expanding, continuing, or under review. Listen for any pacing, discipline, or review language around new partner support. And listen for neocloud credit quality and customer concentration, the transmission channel through which a leadership transition reaches the rest of the complex. GOVERNANCE AND LEADERSHIP The board said on November 13 that it is selecting a search firm and has not formally engaged any candidate. On the call: is a firm named, are criteria stated, is a timeline offered or refused, and do the stated criteria echo the congressional chairs' demand for leadership that makes national security the top priority. Watch Kress's register. Operator language is decisions, allocations, timelines. Caretaker language is continuity, stability, process. The market will grade the difference even if no one says so. Watch for any reference to Huang, any update on the board's November 8 independent investigation, and any severance, equity, or clawback terms that the November 12 filing did not disclose. And watch the analysts: who asks the first succession question, and how many follow, tells you whether the street is treating this as a fundamentals print or a governance print. One more piece of context: this call is management's last scheduled public appearance before the December congressional calendar, the interview deadline, the Teter session, and the public hearing. Any question about Congress gets a decline. The decline is free. Anything beyond it is news. IN THE 10-Q, AFTER THE CALL - How the November 9 securities class action is described, and whether any accrual appears. - Any new disclosure of a government inquiry, subpoena, or investigation. - The subsequent events note, and risk factor changes against last quarter, read word by word. - The legal proceedings and commitments notes are the only places the insurance and indemnification story can surface. Check them. Expect nothing. Be surprised correctly if there is something. THE QUESTIONS THAT MATTER 1. Does the preliminary fiscal 2028 growth expectation of about 70 percent still stand? 2. Where do supply commitments stand now, and how much is memory? 3. Is any China data center revenue in the Q4 outlook, and what is the status of H200 licensing? 4. What revenue is exposed to the remote access and chip security legislation? 5. What has changed in end-use verification for cloud partners in the last 90 days? 6. What is the current total of guarantees and partner support, and is the board reviewing the pace? 7. The August financing platforms: expanding, continuing, or under review? 8. CEO search: firm, criteria, timeline? 9. Any severance, equity, or clawback arrangements with Mr. Huang beyond what has been filed? 10. Any inquiry or subpoena from the Commerce Department, the Justice Department, or the SEC on export compliance? 11. Status and expected timeline of the board's November 8 investigation? 12. Is the 71 to 72 percent margin trough still the fiscal Q4 expectation, and what drives the recovery after it? 13. How much of the quarter, and of the guide, is sovereign AI demand, the category most exposed to the export rule fight and the one management has always liked to showcase? READING THE OUTCOMES Clean print, guide at the bogey, the 2028 language intact, operator tone: the institution is bigger than the man, and the market starts pricing the successor's Nvidia instead of the founder's absence. Soft guide or qualified language: the transition tax is real and gets priced over quarters, not days. A hard guide down or caretaker tone: the print stops being about the quarter at all, and every open question, the search, the investigation, the legislation, the litigation, reprices at once. The founder is gone. Tuesday night is the first evidence of what exactly left with him.

items.title: $NVDA $MU $SNDK $LITE WHAT HAPPENS TO THE $500B CONSORTIUM Short answer: it does not unwind. It decelerates, it gets more expensive, and it gets governed. The headline number was a
items.body: $NVDA $MU $SNDK $LITE WHAT HAPPENS TO THE $500B CONSORTIUM Short answer: it does not unwind. It decelerates, it gets more expensive, and it gets governed. The headline number was a Jensen number. The capital is not. Start with what the consortium actually is. The August platforms with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR are independent financing vehicles meant to mobilize over $500B of third-party capital into AI compute infrastructure. Mobilize is the operative word. $500B was never wired. It was a target that depended on a continuous flow of new deals, and the flow depended on one man standing in the middle of it. The committed capital stays. Those six firms are not charities and they are not Jensen's friends. They are asset managers whose economics run on infrastructure cash flows, contracted offtake, and GPU collateral that has held its value. LP money does not get recalled because a CEO resigns, and performing vehicles keep funding. Anyone predicting the consortium collapses is wrong. What dies is the origination, and origination was the whole story. The platforms were underwritable at that scale because Nvidia supplied three things no contract fully captured: demand visibility years out, allocation priority for the vehicles' projects, and the implicit assurance that the ecosystem's central bank would keep the music playing. All three were personal to Jensen. He was the Bank of Nvidia. An interim CFO and a board under a securities class action cannot reissue that assurance, and would not if they could. So expect three changes. First, velocity. No new headline platforms get announced while the CEO seat is empty, and deal approvals that used to take a phone call now take a committee. The machine keeps running. It just runs at institutional speed instead of Jensen speed. Second, terms. Without the implicit backstop, the sponsors reprice. The marginal buyer of compute, the neoclouds and the second tier data center developers, pays more for capital or does not get it. We already have an early data point: this week QTS cut a planned private debt sale from roughly $800M to roughly $300M. That is the financing channel repricing in real time, before any headline forces it. Third, governance. A board defending a securities lawsuit does not expand the one structure every critic already calls circular vendor financing. Expect a quiet review of the platforms, tighter disclosure, more distance between Nvidia and the vehicles, and a permanent CEO who treats the whole apparatus as a liability to be managed rather than an empire to be extended. Layer on the regulatory side and it tightens further. A meaningful share of what these platforms fund is neocloud and overseas capacity, which is precisely what the remote access bills and chip tracking proposals are aimed at. Sponsors price that cliff whether or not the bills pass this session. The tells to watch: whether Kress mentions the financing partnerships on Tuesday's call, whether any of the six partners publicly reaffirms while the seat is empty, whether a platform lapses without a successor, and whether the next CEO keeps the financing function at Jensen's scale or folds it into ordinary treasury discipline. Your label is right about the origination. It was a mafia in the structural sense: loyalty and flow organized around one man. But the money is institutional, and institutional money does not leave. It just stops moving fast. What Jensen built in a phone call, his successors will administer in a process. The $500B was the process running at his speed. At theirs, it is a smaller, slower, more expensive machine, and the difference between those two numbers is the real size of the man.

The expansion extends AI infrastructure demand beyond U.S. hyperscaler campuses, with implications for local power, cooling and connectivity investment. This is a multiyear development plan, not capacity already delivered or equipment orders already booked. • Telus has withdrawn from co-developing Westbank’s two Vancouver AI data centres. Westbank says both projects will proceed with a new, undisclosed partner, so this is not a confirmed cancellation. Telus still plans to expand Kamloops to 20 MW by end-2028. The distinction matters: individual project partnerships can unwind without signalling a wholesale retreat from Canadian compute investment. • An estimated 6,000 people marched in Edinburgh against large-scale AI data centres, demanding community involvement in approvals. Scotland’s grid-connection queue includes 28 proposals representing 8.9 GW—not committed operating capacity. The government says new planning guidance is due before year-end. The investment risk is permitting friction and longer development timelines, not a newly enacted blanket construction ban.

This demo runs the full fx CLI as WebAssembly compiled with the Zig toolchain. Networking is delegated to browser fetch , and every SDK aspect is configurable in the docs .

fx is a coding agent harness and CLI written in Zig, optimized for research and embeddability as part of larger systems.

It focuses on minimalism and performance across the board, from system prompt design to its tools, feature set, and 6.33 MiB binary.

Its output is closer to a Unix shell than an IDE in the terminal.

It is open source (Apache-2.0), model-agnostic, and suitable for both local and cloud inference.

Install one binary for your terminal, CI, or agent sandbox.

Start an interactive session or run a single request with fx ask . No background service is required.

Run the agent or terminal in the browser with libfx . Your application controls storage, tools, and network access.

fx preserves scroll history and keeps tool activity in the conversation. Open the full transcript when you need more detail.

Concise tool schemas keep the context small. Skill instructions and MCP tool schemas load when needed.

Embed the core with libfx , add your own tools, and connect skills or MCP servers.

Designed to work with local models , gateways , direct provider API access or subscriptions .

items.title: A reminder for everyone in these markets. There is NO shame in selling at a loss. Over the last month or two I sold off a few names in the red, and the market has only gotten worse
items.body: A reminder for everyone in these markets. There is NO shame in selling at a loss. Over the last month or two I sold off a few names in the red, and the market has only gotten worse since. Those were not my proudest trades, but every one of them protected capital that I still have today, ready to deploy on my terms. Your entry price means nothing to the market. The only question that matters is whether you would buy the stock today at this price with this information. If the answer is no, you are not “waiting to break even,” you are holding someone else’s mistake out of pride. Losses are tuition. Blown accounts are dropping out. Protect your capital first, the opportunities always come to those who still have it.

items.title: In some ways the new Fable is a monster. This is SimpleQA Verified from Epoch. There are few benchmarks like this where Fable 5.2 jaggedly jumped ahead of the entire pack. For me t
items.body: In some ways the new Fable is a monster. This is SimpleQA Verified from Epoch. There are few benchmarks like this where Fable 5.2 jaggedly jumped ahead of the entire pack. For me there are two big indicators arriving next week that will tell us a lot about the shape of things going into 2027. I'm assuming two things happen next week: Anthropic releases their internal progress report (from which we will get updated numbers on RSI), and OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra. With the new Astra, we will see how OpenAI answers Fable, and Fable needs to be answered. They need to close the gap, but they also need to close the gap that doesn’t show up on benchmarks: that a lot of people love working with the new Anthropic models, particularly Opus 5.5. And this is starting to tip the table a little. Also expect another huge math release simultaneously with the new Astra. The previous one took five weeks and produced 700 papers; they've had another five weeks since then. They have also been working on other Millennium problems. Don't be shocked by anything. Astra's capability, and if it catches or surpasses Fable, is the first one. The second is where Anthropic is on AL4. The AI Futures Project (the AI 2027 guys) predict that AL4 reached 50% last month. If that's true, that means it will probably hit 80% by January. And at that point, assuming the overall pattern holds, some of the work at Anthropic will be at AL5 - aka fully autonomous with no human input. Probably about 5–10% of work at Anthropic would be at that level. If this number is actually higher than 50%, then things are moving even faster than believed, and that would be a big update for a lot of people, including me, who already has pretty short timelines. Above AL4 50% in October would probably mean RSI before the end of the year. Or possibly, already. So, a very important week for finding out where we are, and where we are headed.

items.title: AI models are inevitably going to keep getting better and better at all coding, tool and computer use, math, and other coding-related tasks. As a result, agents that can use softwa
items.body: AI models are inevitably going to keep getting better and better at all coding, tool and computer use, math, and other coding-related tasks. As a result, agents that can use software to do their work, or generate code from scratch, will improve at a faster rate than all other domains of knowledge work. On one hand that could mean that only a small subset of work can get automated. But probably what happens is that more and more work just becomes coding-shaped to adapt to what agents are good at. You can see it in the most recent examples of model releases in the past couple of months, where agents can generate code that becomes animated videos, games, 3D models for products, and so on. We also know that tool use gives agents the ability to work with much of the same software that people already work with. This helps in cyber, life sciences, finance, and a number of other domains. Our mental model traditionally has been that the models have to be able to know everything about anything to generate value, but in reality they *really* have to know how to use or generate software effectively combined with deep domain expertise to make the right judgment calls inside of workflows. When you have that powerful combination, almost everything else gets unlocked. This is why the acceleration of agents in knowledge work is only going to increase from here.

Management is also calling the $325M of asset-light revenue a one-time thing. Do you really think it can't happen again? Sometimes I feel like Nebius management stays conservative on purpose so they can beat their own guidance. They even called the $12–13B guide for 2027 conservative. And they're getting to break-even faster than you'd expect from a company spending this much. Customers now prepay more than 100% of the capex on new deals, the AI cloud business runs at a 53% EBITDA margin, and management is targeting pre-tax break-even by the end of 2027 while spending $40–45B. When the company breaks even, most of the upside will already be priced into the stock. I won’t wait until then, I’ll do like institutional players do, buy cheap and hold for as long as it makes sense.

The little guy wins. Sure the pod🐒’s are 1.5x more productive, but the random mercenary running their own capital just narrowed the gap massively vs. the institutions. items.title: NVIDIA: LITIGATION HISTORY AND THE SIDE C QUESTION (1/3) Date: November 14, 2026 Grades used throughout: VERIFIED means a primary document (filing, court order, executed agreement,
items.body: NVIDIA: LITIGATION HISTORY AND THE SIDE C QUESTION (1/3) Date: November 14, 2026 Grades used throughout: VERIFIED means a primary document (filing, court order, executed agreement, SEC release) states it. REPORTED means a credible secondary source states it and no primary document was located. NOT FOUND means the searches returned nothing. ESTIMATE means a figure constructed from market benchmarks, labeled as such. BOTTOM LINE • Nvidia historically carried entity securities coverage inside a conventional layered D&O tower: its early 2000s tower contained a policy written around securities claims, the entity slot in that era's standard ABC form. • Nvidia has been sued in four federal securities class actions and has never settled one, so no insurer has ever funded a securities settlement for it, and the absence of such a payment proves nothing about coverage either way. • Its one documented fight with its D&O carriers was offensive, not defensive: in 2005 Nvidia sued its own carriers when they resisted paying defense costs on the 3dfx creditor claims. • Today the Financial Times reports a Side A only program, which, if accurate, is a change from Nvidia's own historical posture; the record does not date the change. • The saving from skipping Sides B and C is on the order of $10M a year (ESTIMATE), about one basis point of Nvidia's roughly $99B of liquidity. It is real money and immaterial at this scale, which is why the absence of entity coverage still needs a reason. 1. THE CURRENT PROGRAM, AS REPORTED The Financial Times (Lee Harris, "Nvidia exposed to possible lawsuits after Jensen Huang's downfall", published November 14, 2026) reports: • Nvidia purchased Side A D&O coverage only, protecting the personal assets of its directors and officers, "up to $900mn in coverage". Quoted from the article: "While Nvidia has in place up to $900mn in coverage protecting the personal assets of its executives and board members, it lacked directors' and officers' (D&O) liability insurance covering the company itself against damages and legal costs stemming from the conduct of its executives, according to two people familiar with its policy." • The program was placed through broker Aon. Insurers named: Beazley, AIG and Chubb. • "But the chipmaker's policy was restricted to Side A and did not include B or C coverage, leaving it potentially exposed to future class-action lawsuits, including 'stock drop' suits." • The size of the Side A coverage ($900M) was first reported by Insurance Insider, per the FT's credit. • Responses: Beazley, Aon and AIG declined to comment. Nvidia and Chubb did not respond. Grade: REPORTED, SINGLE SOURCE. The structure rests on two anonymous people familiar with the policy; the $900M figure is credited one step further upstream to Insurance Insider, whose original item is paywalled and was not reached. Every downstream item found on November 14, 2026 (Traders Union, CNN Brasil, and others) is expressly derivative of the FT. There is no second independent source. The filings silence: an EDGAR full text search across all Nvidia filings (CIK 0001045810) returns zero hits ever for "Side A", "Side B" or "Side C". The FY2026 10-K (filed February 25, 2026), the Q2 FY2027 10-Q (filed August 26, 2026), the 2026 proxy, the November 12, 2026 8-K and the 2025 S-3ASR disclose nothing about insurance structure. The 2026 proxy confirms indemnity agreements with directors and officers are in force. The one operative filed document, the 2006 form of indemnity agreement (EX-10.1), contractually requires the company to obtain and maintain D&O insurance naming the directors and officers as insureds, with a six year run-off endorsement if cover lapses; it names no sides, limits, broker or carriers. D&O program structure is not an SEC disclosure item for any issuer, so the silence is normal and neither confirms nor refutes the FT. Grade: VERIFIED as to what the filings say and omit. Context on rarity, for scale only: a broker survey reported by the FT (WTW, 2018) found more than 80 percent of surveyed public companies bought Sides B and C as well as A, and named practitioners in the FT describe Side A only as "very seldom" bought. A separate survey of very large companies documents standalone Side A buyers typically carrying $50M to $200M of limit, far below the reported $900M. Grade: REPORTED. 2. NVIDIA LITIGATION HISTORY: THE FOUR ENTITY SECURITIES CLASS ACTIONS A suit against the company for securities violations is the Side C type event by definition, regardless of who paid. Nvidia's complete federal securities class action history from its 1999 IPO to November 14, 2026 is four cases. 2.1 THE 2002 ACCOUNTING CLASS ACTIONS (CONSOLIDATED, N.D. CAL.) • Filing: first action filed February 19, 2002; approximately 14 actions followed and were consolidated. Class period February 15, 2000 to February 14, 2002. • Allegation: securities law violations arising from Nvidia's February 14, 2002 announcement of an internal investigation of accounting matters; the resulting restatement covered fiscal 2000, fiscal 2001, and the first three quarters of fiscal 2002. • Outcome: dismissed with prejudice in stages across 2003 (March 28, June 12 and August 21, 2003 orders), announced by Nvidia on August 22, 2003. No settlement. • Who paid: nobody. A dismissal with prejudice generates no settlement fund and no insurer contribution. • Sources: Nvidia Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 26, 2003, Legal Proceedings; Nvidia press release, August 22, 2003. Grade: VERIFIED. 2.2 IN RE NVIDIA CORP. SECURITIES LITIGATION, 2008 (GPU DEFECT) • Filing: September 2008, N.D. Cal., No. 3:08-cv-04260-RS. Class period November 8, 2007 to July 2, 2008. • Allegation: Sections 10(b) and 20(a); the defendants concealed unusually high failure rates in mobile GPU products caused by a weak die and packaging material set, and the financial impact, until the July 2, 2008 announcement of a $150M to $200M charge (the FY2009 10-K records the charge at $196.0M). • Outcome: dismissed without leave to amend on October 12, 2011 for failure to plead scienter; affirmed by the Ninth Circuit, 768 F.3d 1046 (2014). No settlement. • Who paid: nobody. • Sources: Stanford Securities Class Action Clearinghouse case record; Order Granting Motion to Dismiss, October 12, 2011. Grade: VERIFIED. 2.3 IN RE NVIDIA CORPORATION SECURITIES LITIGATION, 2018 (CRYPTOCURRENCY) • Filing: December 21, 2018, N.D. Cal., No. 4:18-cv-07669-HSG; amended complaint May 13, 2020. Class period August 10, 2017 to November 15, 2018. • Allegation: Sections 10(b) and 20(a); false and misleading statements about channel inventory and the impact of cryptocurrency mining demand on GPU sales, and about the company's ability to withstand crypto volatility through gaming demand. • Outcome: still pending after a full appellate cycle. Dismissed without leave to amend March 2, 2021; reversed by the Ninth Circuit in August 2023; the Supreme Court granted certiorari in June 2024 and dismissed the writ as improvidently granted on December 11, 2024; class certified March 25, 2026. No settlement reported as of the latest reliable coverage in October 2026, and Nvidia's Q3 FY2026 10-Q records none. • Who paid: nobody to date. This is the first Nvidia securities case in history to survive into a posture where a settlement is realistically possible, and it has not settled. • Regulatory companion, kept in its own lane: on May 6, 2022 the SEC announced settled charges against Nvidia for inadequate cryptomining disclosures in FY2018, with a cease and desist order and a $5.5M penalty paid by the company (SEC Press Release 2022-79). An SEC penalty is not a Side C loss and is not insurable under any structure; the payment was Nvidia's. Grade: VERIFIED. • Sources: Nvidia FY2022 10-K and Q3 FY2026 10-Q, Legal Proceedings; SEC Press Release 2022-79. Grades: VERIFIED; class certification date REPORTED (multiple outlets). 2.4 KISTENMACHER V. NVIDIA CORPORATION, 2026 • Filing: November 9, 2026, N.D. Cal., Case No. 5:26-cv-13448. Class period October 9, 2025 to November 8, 2026. PSLRA lead plaintiff deadline January 8, 2027. • Allegation: Sections 10(b) and 20(a) over statements about the Huang relationship and related governance, national security, and export compliance risk. The complaint contains zero mentions of insurance and zero mentions of indemnification, and seeks unspecified damages. • Outcome: pending. No settlement, no payment. • Who paid: nobody. Under the program the FT reported on November 14, 2026, the company's own loss in this case would be uninsured; that is a statement about the current program only. • Sources: the complaint, Document 1. Grade: VERIFIED; the plaintiff firm alert of November 10, 2026 is REPORTED. The never settled fact, stated plainly: across four securities class actions spanning 24 years, Nvidia has never settled one. Two were dismissed outright, one is pending in a settlement capable posture for the first time, and one was filed this month. Any argument that begins "look at who paid Nvidia's settlements" has no settlements to point to.

items.body: OPTICAL NETWORKING DAILY DIGEST, SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 14, 2026 STATUS CHANGE • Cisco Systems: Cisco's first quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call on November 12, 2026 added vendor-stated optics detail to the results reported on November 12, 2026. In prepared remarks, CEO Charles Robbins stated that in the quarter Cisco secured 3 new AI design wins, two for P200 powered systems in data center interconnect and scale-across use cases, and "The third was for 1.6 Terabit Optics for scale-out use case." In Q&A, Robbins stated: "The design win we had this quarter at the 1.6 Terabit optic was a client side win. And it was our first client side optics win at this particular hyperscaler." The hyperscaler was not named. CFO Mark Patterson stated on optics: "We actually had a $1 billion quarter, just last quarter on the optic side," referring to the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, and said the first quarter of fiscal 2027 was a record first quarter for optics. On timing, the multi-rail optical system is expected in the first few months of calendar 2027, and the USFP (Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable) platform, being developed with NVIDIA for 4x the bandwidth density and 1.3x the power efficiency of current models, with an open industry specification planned, is "a couple of years out, probably a few years out." The scale-across architecture was described as combining Silicon One P200 deep-buffered systems, market-leading Acacia coherent optics, and open line systems. A trade press summary of the call had reported that Acacia 800G-ZR revenue passed 400G-ZR; the full call transcript contains no mention of ZR or 800G products at all, so that claim is not corroborated by the call itself. No new product announcement, part number, pricing, or GA date was stated. https://t.co/W9rGgX28Nx

If you freak out every time a volatile* stock swings 5–10%, you’ll end up trading the price action rather than the underlying thesis… I think Dmitry Balyasny made a great point in an interview: the optimal approach lies somewhere between trading and investing. Focus too much on daily price action and you start questioning your thesis every time the stock moves against you. Hold something for three years and you risk rationalizing why the market still hasn’t recognized what you think you see…
