items.title: https://t.co/DrLGfxIj3m GAI DATA CENTER DEVELOPMENT DAILY DIGEST, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 13, 2026 LEAD ITEMS • CleanMax and Neysa Green Compute Factory, Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh,
items.body: https://t.co/DrLGfxIj3m GAI DATA CENTER DEVELOPMENT DAILY DIGEST, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 13, 2026 LEAD ITEMS • CleanMax and Neysa Green Compute Factory, Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh, India: an operator MoU signed 11/12/26 will power a 2 GW compute factory, with Neysa anchoring 1 GW of IT load. Detail under NEW LAUNCHES. NEW LAUNCHES • CleanMax and Neysa Green Compute Factory, Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh, India, LATE, event 11/12/26, confirmed, verified. CleanMax signed an MoU with the Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board to build 3 GW of wind and solar plus 1 GW of pumped hydro to power a 2 GW Green Compute Factory, with Neysa anchoring the park with 1 GW of IT load. The roughly Rs 50,000 crore figure is the power side, not a campus cost. A reported Orvakal location and a 03/28 target are single-source and were not adopted. No pin was verified. • ReNew Green Hyperscale Data Centre, Anakapalli, Andhra Pradesh, India, LATE, event 11/12/26, corroborated, verified. ReNew announced a 1 GW green hyperscale data centre at Anakapalli, Rs 67,000 crore of an Rs 80,000 crore state package. No tenant or timeline was named. Coverage explicitly distinguishes this from ReNew's separate Makavaripalem 1,000 MW project; the two were not merged, and Makavaripalem is not tracked under that name. • Google Ozans-Chateauroux Data Center Campus, Etrechet, Indre, France, LATE, event 11/02/26, confirmed, verified. The CNDP consultation dossier was published for a campus of about 195 hectares: Phase 1 first building on a 225 kV connection at 120 MW, Phase 2 from 2031 on a 400 kV connection, at EUR 8.6 billion. Announced campus MW is UNKNOWN as a total: the 120 MW figure is the Phase 1 grid connection, and a secondary 1,320 MW figure is a grid connection figure, not campus MW. Building counts differ between the two primary sources (8 to 10 per CNDP, 6 to 8 per RTE) and are not reconciled. No pin was verified. PROJECT EVOLUTIONS • Fermi Project Matador Campus, Amarillo, Texas, United States, event 11/13/26, single-source, candidate. The Financial Times reported that the unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler behind the 600 MW prepayment is Amazon. Fermi has not named the customer and Amazon has not confirmed; the FT original was not read. No lease is signed and no MW, stage, or timeline on file changes. • Meta Sturgeon County AI Data Center, Sturgeon County, Alberta, Canada, LATE, event 11/10/26, corroborated, verified. The campus clears its federal hurdle: the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada ruled it cannot be designated for federal impact assessment because construction has substantially begun (grading, roadwork, gas-line relocations, and utilities under way since 06/26), consistent with the on-file under_construction phase. It is not an environmental approval. • AWS Wheatfield Data Center Campus, Wheatfield, Indiana, United States, LATE, event 11/12/26, single-source, candidate. Amazon broke ground on the tracked campus, reported at $7 billion. A stage signal toward ground_broken; no census stage changes on a single local report. • Syntys data center campus, Doha, Qatar, LATE, event 11/12/26, single-source, candidate. Syntys (Ooredoo) broke ground on a 20 MW Tier III facility on an existing campus, with the Minister of Communications attending. Below the 100 MW launch floor; captured as an evolution of an existing campus, not a launch. • Oscar Renda Contracting data center site contracts, Mid-Atlantic and Southwest, United States, event 11/13/26, single-source, candidate. Site-work pass, contractor-out: Southland Holdings announced master service agreements for labor and equipment at two unnamed data center sites. The release's $34 million figure is a separate tunnel project and is not attached to the data center work. A contractor signal only; no campus stage move. • Soluna Project Kati 2, Willacy County, Texas, United States, event 11/13/26, unverified, candidate, lead. A CEO interview cited on X floats nearly $4 billion and a Q2 2028 target. Grounding confirms the campus (a 112 MW building filing at about $471.8 million, and a 350 MW full-campus JV target) but not those two figures, which ship as lead only. BLOCKERS • Fermi Project Matador Campus, Amarillo, Texas, United States, LATE, disclosed 11/12/26, termination dated 11/10/26 in the 10-Q, corroborated. Fermi and TensorWave terminated the 222 MW lease and the AMD credit support tied to it; the lease never took effect because closing conditions, including project financing, were never met. Fermi ends the quarter with zero signed leases, offset in the same disclosure by the prepayment under FINANCING ITEMS. This is a touch on verified finding 1049. • Nebius Vineland Data Center (DataOne build), Vineland, New Jersey, United States, LATE, event 11/12/26, corroborated, verified. The remaining Microsoft tranches slip to Q2 2027 against the on-file 2025 to 2026 rollout, because DataOne wound down temporary generation faster than expected ahead of Bloom Energy fuel cells. Nebius cut 2026 revenue guidance by $200 million citing third-party site delays. The Microsoft contract was not reported cancelled. The primary letter was read through trade reporting; the 6-K was not retrieved in metadata-only mode. • Cerebras Systems contracted capacity (operator-level, no tracked campus named), LATE, event 11/12/26, corroborated, candidate. Cerebras said its initial OpenAI tranches are behind schedule on land, power, and shell delays, with delay credits deducted and catch-up not projected until H2 2027; 700 MW is now under contract for delivery by end 2027. No campus is named, so no census change can be staged. REGULATORY RESTRICTIONS • Independence, Missouri, United States, event 11/13/26, confirmed, verified. The City Council approved a 180-day moratorium on new data center and battery storage applications while the city reviews its business, zoning, fire, building, and development rules. The tracked Nebius Independence campus is expressly exempted. Caveat: the city release does not state a separate council meeting date, so the event date rests on the release date. • Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States, LATE, event 11/12/26, single-source, candidate. The City Council passed the data center ordinance 7 to 6; a full ban failed. New data centers need council approval and are allowed only in existing buildings. The ordinance goes to the mayor; the existing moratorium expires 11/21/26. • Boise, Idaho, United States, LATE, event 11/10/26, corroborated, verified. The City Council unanimously imposed a six-month moratorium (emergency ordinance ORD-45-26) on facilities of 100,000 sq ft or more, or 20 MW or more. The city reports no large applications pending, and the proposed Blacks Creek campus on federal land is not reached. Surfaced by the X sweep and grounded the same run. • Oakley, California, United States, LATE, event 11/10/26, single-source, candidate. The City Council voted 3 to 1 to introduce an ordinance banning data centers of all sizes in all zoning districts. Adoption is expected in 12/26, superseding the existing moratorium. • Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, United States, LATE, event 11/11/26, single-source, candidate. The Council voted to extend the moratorium on new data center rezoning requests through the end of 2027 or until the zoning code is updated, with one pipeline exception for an approved hyperscale rezoning. • Boulder County, Colorado, United States, LATE, event 11/10/26, single-source, candidate. Commissioners adopted rules capping data center IT load at 50 kilowatts in unincorporated areas, restricted to light and general industrial districts with limited-impact special review, ending the 06/02/26 application moratorium. • New Jersey, United States, LATE, event 11/10/26, single-source, candidate. The BPU extended the written response deadline in the Data Center Fair Share Act proceeding, Docket EO26080463, from 11/13/26 to 12/14/26. An information-gathering docket, not a tariff adoption; the BPU's own notice was not retrieved. • United States (federal), LATE, event 11/09/26, corroborated, candidate. The Senate cloture vote of 73 to 25 advanced the BAAJA permitting reform bill (S.5653) to floor debate; reported data center provisions include developer-paid grid upgrades for projects of 20 MW or more and a 150-day legal challenge limit. The bill text was not read; nothing here is enacted law. • United States (federal), LATE, event 11/11/26, single-source, candidate. Senator Hawley called for a nationwide moratorium until Congress passes a bill of rights on rate increases, the first Senate Republican to do so. A political call, not a filed bill; the Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez moratorium act remains the pending vehicle. • Kansas, United States, LATE, event 11/12/26, single-source, candidate. Governor-elect Holscher, who campaigned on a statewide moratorium pledge, won the governor's race. The pledge is not in force: she takes office in 01/27 and any pause needs an order, budget, or bill. • New Braunfels, Texas, United States, event 11/09/26 (first reading), single-source, watch, review 11/17/26. Draft ordinance ORD26-367 would require heavy industrial zoning plus a special use permit, a 2,000-foot buffer, a 50-acre minimum, and closed-loop cooling. Second reading is 11/16/26. Correction to the X post that surfaced it: the draft minimum is 50 acres, not the 100 acres a public commenter asked for. • Arizona, United States, LATE, event 11/12/26, unverified, candidate, lead. An X post says state officials plan to take up a data center moratorium in the coming session. Context is grounded (the AG has called for one since 08/26 and a three-year pause on new tax incentive applications runs through 06/29), but the specific 11/12/26 joint plan is not grounded in any non-X source found. • Maine, United States, event 11/13/26, unverified, candidate, lead. An X post says lawmakers are preparing new proposals including a moratorium. Grounding corrects the timing of the history it cites: Governor Mills vetoed LD 307 on 04/24/26 and the override failed 04/29/26. No non-X source confirms new November proposals. • Atlanta metro, Georgia, United States, LATE, Q3 2026 summary, single-source, candidate. A tracker post claims 13 Atlanta-area governments adopted or extended moratoria in Q3 2026. The count itself was not verified; components are grounded (Douglas County denied a rezoning on 07/07/26; Coweta County adopted a moratorium in 05/26), and a Georgia tracker lists 66 local measures statewide, 53 in force. Captured as late-surfacing context only. COMMUNITY ISSUES • Project Delta, Walnut Cove, Stokes County, North Carolina, United States, LATE, event 11/12/26, single-source, candidate. Residents and community groups sued Stokes County a second time over the 09/14/26 rezoning of nearly 1,850 acres, alleging a rushed, deficient analysis and no confirmed water source, and asking the court to void the rezoning. The county votes 11/23/26 on a 15-year development agreement. The complaint itself was not read; the allegations are the plaintiffs' characterizations. • Circle T Data Center Campus, Westlake, Texas, United States, LATE, event 11/12/26, corroborated, verified. The Town Council unanimously approved the development agreement for the 1.1 million sq ft campus, a week after the Keller settlement ended the lawsuit. The settlement obliges nearly $1.9 million in payments within 45 days and noise limits of 49 dB overnight and 56 dB daytime. This closes the 11/12/26 run's unretrieved Westlake outcome. • Raceway Energy Campus, Carbon County, Utah, United States, LATE, event 11/12/26, corroborated, verified. The Planning Commission approved the conditional use permit 5 to 1 as about 200 residents turned out in opposition, some removed by deputies. The permit carries 26 conditions, including no culinary water for cooling and 70 dB noise limits at residences. The campus is about 640 acres of state trust land for nuclear, fuel manufacturing, and data center facili

C. C. Wei is already in his 70s, and has been holding the concurrent Chairman and CEO roles at TSMC since June 2024 when former Chairman Mark Liu retired.
